head: b802686
note: Read-only hunt over the round-5 tree — the round whose whole job was fixing round 4. Committed BEFORE any fixing. Finders were additionally required to list every file their suggested fix would touch (fix_touches), which is lesson L-052 turned into a schema field.

findings.title: The recorded residual "served once" understates the recovery window: the same captured body is served repeatedly, and each serving hands out a full rotating refresh token
findings.requirement: spec P3 / docs/Threat_Model.md T20; L-050 ("say in the code what an attacker gets inside that window"); L-053 (when code and prose disagree, decide which is TRUE)
findings.mechanism: The residual comment at apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:276-280 states that "inside the window a captured request body ... is served once, and the tablet is then unpaired on its next refresh". Neither half of "served once" holds. (a) A recovery rewrites only `replaced_by` on the row the id consumed (child-auth.ts:309); its `used_at` and `used_request_id` are left standing, and `used_at` is deliberately never advanced (child-auth.ts:306), so the predicate at child-auth.ts:281-286 keeps matching the SAME body for the whole two minutes — each pass finds the new head unclaimed and issues another pair of tokens. (b) What a serving returns is not merely a 15-minute access token: child-auth.ts:329 returns `next.token`, minted by `issueRefreshToken` (child-auth.ts:33-38) with a full `childRefreshTtlSeconds` and no marker of any kind, so the replayer can rotate it down the ORDINARY path at child-auth.ts:357-361 — no id needed, no window, no audit row — for as long as the session lives. Nothing server-side ends that chain; the reuse revocation at child-auth.ts:334 fires only when the real tablet next presents its own (now-retired) token, which on a sleeping or powered-off tablet can be many hours later. The same understatement is copied into docs/Threat_Model.md:46 ("served once and is then audited and visible, which is the recorded residual") and into docs/Progress.md:116, so the record a reader relies on for the size of this hole is wrong in the direction that makes it look smaller.
findings.user_impact: A parent or reviewer reading the code, the threat model or the progress record is told that a stolen refresh request body buys an attacker one served response. It actually buys a self-renewing child session that lasts until the child's tablet next refreshes — overnight, or a whole weekend for a tablet that is put away — during which the attacker can read the child's profile, homework and rewards. The size of an accepted child-privacy residual is recorded smaller than it is.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and ruled out: (1) nothing marks the consumed row as recovery-spent — the only write to it after a recovery is `replaced_by` at child-auth.ts:309, and BUG-249's fix nulls `used_request_id` on the REPLACEMENT (child-auth.ts:307), not on the row the id consumed; (2) repetition is already demonstrated in-tree by the passing case 'a second lost response in a row still recovers, through the same id' (apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:324-333), which serves the identical body three times; (3) the token a recovery returns is indistinguishable from an ordinary rotation's — `issueRefreshToken` sets only session_id/token_hash/issued_at/expires_at (child-auth.ts:33-38) and `used_at is null`, so the `if (row.used_at)` gate at child-auth.ts:251 is skipped entirely on its next use; (4) `RATE_RULES.childRefreshPerSession` (60/hour, rate-limit.ts:119) bounds the RATE of those rotations, not their duration; (5) no existing test asserts that a second recovery of the same body is refused.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide which statement is true and make the other match (L-053). Minimum: rewrite child-auth.ts:276-280, docs/Threat_Model.md T20 and the BUG-248 residual in docs/Bug_Ledger.md / docs/Progress.md to say what the code does — inside the window a captured body can be served repeatedly, and each serving yields a live rotating refresh token, so the replayer holds the child's session until the tablet's next refresh revokes it. If the lead wants the smaller residual the record claims, make the recovery genuinely single-use per attempt (e.g. stamp a `recovered_at` on the consumed row and add `recovered_at is null` to the predicate at child-auth.ts:281-286) and keep the 'second lost response in a row' case green by letting the retry recover through the head of the lineage instead; that needs a new column, so it is a migration decision, not a fixer's.

findings.title: The audit row that is the whole compensating control for BUG-248's residual reaches no reader: nothing in the product selects from audit_events, and the log line is info level
findings.requirement: BUG-248 lead decision (2): "Write an AUDIT event on every recovery ... so a replay is visible to the family and to ops instead of silent"
findings.mechanism: child-auth.ts:315-320 inserts `child_session.refresh_recovered` and the comments at child-auth.ts:278-279 and :315-316 justify it as making a replay "visible to the family and to ops instead of silent"; docs/Threat_Model.md:46 carries the same claim as T20's mitigation. No code path reads that row. `grep -rn 'audit_events' apps/api/src` returns inserts only — there is no route, admin or family, that selects from public.audit_events — and no web or mobile screen reads it either. The only other signal is `deps.log({ level: 'info', event: 'child_refresh_recovered' })` at child-auth.ts:310-314; the one log event in this same file that is meant to be alerted on uses `level: 'error'` (`pairing_failure_budget_exhausted`, child-auth.ts:129). So for the family the event is silent in the product, and for ops it is an info line among all other info lines with nothing raising it.
findings.repro: Static, and checkable in one command: `grep -rn "audit_events" apps/api/src apps/web/src apps/mobile/src | grep -v "insert into"` returns no reader. Behaviourally: run the existing case '[repro] the same token and the same request id issues tokens instead of revoking' (apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:300), then call every parent-facing route the app uses (GET /v1/family, /v1/devices, /v1/children/*) and no response mentions the recovery; `api.logs` contains one entry at level 'info'.
findings.user_impact: A family whose child's refresh body was captured and replayed is told, by the product, nothing at all — the tablet simply asks to be connected again on its next refresh, exactly as it did before BUG-244. The mitigation the threat model credits for making a high-severity residual acceptable does not deliver a signal to either audience it names.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked: the RLS policy `audit_member_read` (supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:520) plus the shim's default privileges (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:107) do let a signed-in parent read the row through the raw Supabase Data API, so the row is not unreadable in principle — but no PencilLift surface performs that read, so no family ever sees it, and that is what "visible to the family" claims. I also confirmed there is no admin reader: apps/api/src/routes/admin-ops.ts and admin-monetization.ts only insert. The existing `child_session.revoked_token_reuse` row has the same property, but that revocation is at least visible to the child as an immediate disconnection; a served recovery has no user-visible consequence at all, which is why this one needs a reader.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) narrow the claim in child-auth.ts:278-279, :315-316 and docs/Threat_Model.md T20 to what is true — the recovery is recorded in audit_events for a later investigation and logged at info, with no family-facing notice — or (b) make one of the two audiences real: raise the log to `level: 'error'` (or 'warn') so it matches the alerting precedent at child-auth.ts:129, and, if the family is to be told, surface it on the parent's device list next to the connected/disconnected state.

findings.title: "Mirrored in secure storage, so an app the OS kills mid-refresh still finishes that refresh" is untrue past two minutes, and the sibling comment in mode.ts already says so
findings.requirement: L-049 (the id is persisted because "process death that a mobile OS causes at will ... is the same lost response from the user's side"); L-053
findings.mechanism: apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:180-183 still asserts that mirroring the pending request in secure storage means "an app the OS kills mid-refresh still finishes that refresh". After this diff it does not: the server only serves such a retry while `now - used_at < RECOVERY_WINDOW_MS` (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:284, two minutes), so a cold start later than that presents an already-rotated token, takes the fallthrough at child-auth.ts:334 and unpairs the tablet — the very BUG-244 harm. The device side even encodes an expectation of much later cold starts: `REQUEST_ID_MAX_AGE_MS` is 10 * 60_000 (child-session.ts:52), five times the server's window, and its docstring justifies the slack as keeping "an id the server would still honour" — true for seconds of clock skew, not for the 2-to-10-minute band, where the server will certainly refuse. The same file's sibling record is the accurate one: apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:43-46 says "the server serves such a retry only briefly after the rotation". The in-tree evidence reinforces the false impression rather than catching it: 'a process killed mid-refresh finishes that same refresh after a cold start' (apps/mobile/src/family/child-session-r2.review.test.ts:485-528) runs with `now` frozen at a single instant, so it demonstrates a relaunch at zero elapsed time, which no real OS kill and relaunch achieves.
findings.repro: Extend the existing cold-start case with elapsed time, as '[repro] an id kept across a long cold start' (child-session-r2.review.type.ts:579) already does, but by three minutes instead of fourteen hours, and drive it against the real route: pair a device, refresh with an id whose response is dropped, advance `api.now.value` by 3 minutes, replay token+id — apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:374-392 already proves the answer is 401 with `revoke_reason = 'refresh_token_reuse'`. That is a tablet the OS killed mid-refresh and that came back three minutes later, and it is unpaired.
findings.user_impact: A reader (or the next fixer) trusts a comment that says the keychain mirror makes an OS-killed refresh finish, and therefore believes BUG-244 is closed for the process-death case that motivated persisting the id at all. In fact only relaunches inside two minutes are covered; a child who closes the tablet and picks it up after break still has to ask a grown-up for a new pairing code.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked that the device-side constant cannot rescue this: whether `requestIdForThisRefresh` (child-session.ts:218-242) adopts the stored id or mints a fresh one, the request still carries the rotated refresh token, so child-auth.ts:281-286 fails on the window either way and child-auth.ts:334 revokes — so this is a prose defect, not a second behavioural one, and I am not re-filing the window itself, which child-auth.ts:279-280 openly records as "exactly the pre-BUG-244 unpairing". I also checked that no test pins the claim in the comment: the only cold-start cases are child-session-r2.review.test.ts:485 (zero elapsed) and :605 (30 s elapsed), both inside two minutes.
findings.suggested_fix: Make child-session.ts:180-183 say what mode.ts:43-46 says — the mirror lets the next process present the SAME id, and the server honours that only briefly after the rotation, so a later relaunch is a new attempt and the tablet is asked to connect again. In the same pass, either bring REQUEST_ID_MAX_AGE_MS down to a value defensible as clock slack over a two-minute server window, or rewrite its docstring so the slack is justified by "never discard an id the server MIGHT still honour" rather than "would still honour", and add one case at 3 minutes elapsed so the boundary is pinned on the device side too.

findings.title: mobile-r2.review.test.ts cites tests/auth.test.ts:189 for the rotation-reuse rule, but the same commit moved that test to line 209
findings.requirement: A reference in a docstring must point at the thing it names (BUG-251's lesson: a comment must not state something the code does not do)
findings.mechanism: apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:267 names `tests/auth.test.ts:189 ("refresh tokens rotate and reuse revokes the session")` as the case that requires immediate revocation. At 8201fa1 that test really was at auth.test.ts:189 (`git show 8201fa1:apps/api/tests/auth.test.ts | grep -n 'refresh tokens rotate'` → 189). The same commit b802686 inserted the `pairCount` / `pairingAddress()` block at auth.test.ts:139-155, above it, so the test is now at auth.test.ts:209 and line 189 is in the middle of the unrelated 'two concurrent redemptions' / 'expired codes' region. The rewritten docstring was edited in this diff without re-deriving the number.
findings.repro: `sed -n '189p' apps/api/tests/auth.test.ts` prints a line from a different test; `grep -n "refresh tokens rotate" apps/api/tests/auth.test.ts` prints 209.
findings.user_impact: The next reviewer asked to check whether the recovery weakens the rotation rule is sent to the wrong line of the wrong test — the exact cost L-053/BUG-251 was filed for, in the docstring that exists to stop that rule being weakened by accident.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Verified against the pre-diff blob, not from memory: the test was at 189 at 8201fa1 and is at 209 at b802686, and the shift is caused by lines this same commit added above it (auth.test.ts:139-155). No other file carries the stale reference (`grep -rn "auth.test.ts:189"` matches only mobile-r2.review.test.ts:267).
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the test by name only, or by file and test name — `tests/auth.test.ts > 'refresh tokens rotate and reuse revokes the session'` — so the reference cannot rot the next time a helper is inserted above it.

findings.title: The case named for the non-uuid stored id never reaches the uuid guard; deleting that guard keeps it green
findings.requirement: L-054 (an assertion is only as good as the value and source it searches; prove a guard bites by removing it)
findings.mechanism: apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:77 is the uuid guard inside `parseStoredRequest`, justified at :75-76 as stopping a stored id the contract would refuse on every attempt from wedging the device. The only case named for it, 'a stored id that is not a uuid is replaced instead of wedging every refresh' (child-session-r2.review.test.ts:534-556), stores the bare string `'not-a-uuid'`. Because the record is now JSON, `JSON.parse('not-a-uuid')` throws and `parseStoredRequest` returns null at child-session.ts:71 — the function returns before line 77 is evaluated. Deleting `|| !uuidSchema.safeParse(id).success` from line 77 therefore leaves the case green, and so does deleting the whole `typeof id !== 'string'` clause for that input. Line 77 is only reachable for a well-formed JSON object whose `id` is not a uuid, and the only writer of that key is child-session.ts:238-240, which always writes `newRequestId()`, so no test in the file drives that branch.
findings.repro: Statically: `parseStoredRequest('not-a-uuid')` returns at child-session.ts:71 (JSON.parse throws), so line 77 never runs for the fixture the case uses. A case that does reach it: `storage.data.set(STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshRequestId, JSON.stringify({ id: 'not-a-uuid', mintedAtMs: Date.parse('2026-09-26T12:00:00.000Z') }))`, then assert the refresh presents the freshly minted uuid — that assertion goes red with line 77's uuid clause removed, and the current one does not.
findings.user_impact: None directly for a child today — the guard is defence in depth and the legacy bare-id case is caught one line earlier. The cost is to the next reader and the next fixer: the file claims a guard is covered when the only evidence for it is a fixture that stops short of it, which is how the four unfalsifiable assertions L-054 was written for got in.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked both halves. (a) That line 71 short-circuits: `'not-a-uuid'` is not valid JSON, and the other legacy shape the comment names — a bare uuid string from an older build — is not valid JSON either, so it also returns at 71, never 77. (b) That no other case in the file reaches line 77: the only writes to STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshRequestId in the test file are child-session-r2.review.test.ts:539 ('not-a-uuid') and :844 (a bare uuid, used only by the unpair case which never calls the parser), and every other stored record comes from the production write at child-session.ts:238-240, which is always a uuid.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a second case that stores a well-formed JSON record with a non-uuid `id` (and, while there, one with a non-numeric `mintedAtMs`) and assert a fresh id is minted, so both clauses of `parseStoredRequest` at child-session.ts:77-78 have a fixture that reddens when the clause is deleted; keep the existing case, renamed for what it actually covers (an older build's non-JSON value).

sweeps_sound: Recovery predicate is a conjunction, not a disjunction: apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:281-286 ANDs id-present, id-match, freshness, replacement-exists and live; a blind replay (no id) and a wrong-id replay both still revoke, pinned by apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:335-345 and :273-285.

The freshness bound can go red, so it is not decoration: deleting apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:284 turns apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:374-392 from 401 into 200 — the mutation the ledger records, re-derived independently.

BUG-249 stays closed: the retired replacement is stamped `used_request_id = null` (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:307), so it cannot satisfy the predicate in its own right (null !== a uuid), and restoring `${refreshRequestId}` there reddens apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:399-410. Tried to find a second path to a live token from the retired row and could not: only the hash is stored (child-auth.ts:33-38).

One clock per comparison holds for the new bound: every write of child_refresh_tokens.used_at in the tree is the request instant or a copy of it (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:359 and :306), and a grep over apps/ and supabase/migrations found no other writer, so `now.getTime() - row.used_at.getTime()` never mixes the Worker clock with now() (child-auth.ts:47-49).

The recovery cannot resurrect a dead session or bypass consent: `row.live` (built from t.expires_at, s.revoked_at/expires_at, d.revoked_at, c.status, f.deleted_at at child-auth.ts:232-233) is a conjunct, and `consented()` is re-checked inside the branch at child-auth.ts:293 exactly as on the ordinary path at :350.

stampDeviceWhenNoLiveSession's new justification is true, checked path by path: /pair always inserts a fresh child_devices row (child-auth.ts:157-160), and archive (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:539-540), consent withdrawal (apps/api/src/routes/guardians.ts:725-728), device revoke (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:596) and deletion (supabase/migrations/0620_deletion_purge.sql:102-105) each revoke the device row alongside the session, so no API path reaches a device row with a second live session (child-auth.ts:59-65).

L-027 is satisfied by the two reworked fixtures: they now build timestamps from the database clock the guard reads (apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:209-212 and :448-451 against `s.expires_at > now()` at child-auth.ts:74), and the harness only pins pencillift.request_now (supabase/tests/harness.ts:120-121) — it does not override now() — so nothing here goes stale on 2026-10-01.

The `not exists` clause still bites: with it removed, both raw-SQL cases (apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:200-219 and :443-455) would see the device stamped and their `revokedAt` null assertions fail.

The pairing-address hygiene cases can fail: mobile-r2 makes 18 pairings before the new describe, so with pairingAddress() removed the 22-device loop at apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:468-472 crosses the 20-per-/64 limit on its third iteration; and the companion case at :474-493 still proves the limit bites (20x404 then 429).

Per-pairing addresses do not quietly disarm the service-wide guess budget: 'ZZZZZZZZ' is a well-formed Crockford code (apps/api/src/auth/pairing.ts:5,16-25) so every attempt really reserves a unit, and the totals (26 failed guesses in auth.test.ts, 21 in mobile-r2) stay far under pairingRedeemFailuresGlobal = 200/hour (apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:117); the varied third group gives a distinct /64 AND a distinct /48 (rate-limit.ts:214-234), which is what the docstrings claim.

L-007 still holds after the wrapper change: both the new pre-resolution in `once` (apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:157) and the request's own fetch go through the single `accessToken`/`inflight` refresher (child-session.ts:286-294), and all four call sites pass the whole session (apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:51, apps/mobile/src/homework/child-api.ts:18, apps/mobile/app/(child)/rewards.tsx:50, apps/mobile/app/(child)/help.tsx:50) whose registered token source IS childSession.accessToken (apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts:53-54), so no call presents a bearer the pre-resolution did not produce.

HUNT5-G-3's fix is falsifiable and the old branch is genuinely gone: removing child-session.ts:157 makes the generation sample precede the call's own refresh again, so apps/mobile/src/family/child-session-r2.review.test.ts:327-359 would see ['access-1','access-1'] and one refresh instead of two. Verified by running the file: 22/22 pass.

The missing age check on the in-memory branch cannot resurrect a finished attempt: every terminal path clears `pendingRequest` (child-session.ts:246 on success and on a refusal, :213 in forget, :314 in pair), so a non-null in-memory record always belongs to a refresh that genuinely has not finished.

Adopting an over-age id costs nothing extra: whether child-session.ts:227-230 adopts or mints, the request still carries the rotated token, so child-auth.ts:281-286 refuses identically — the docstring's "the slack only ever ADMITS an id" is accurate.

The unconditional storage write is correctly ordered and correctly dated: it happens before the request goes out and keeps the MINT instant, not the write instant (child-session.ts:232-241), so an id rewritten on every retry still ages; making it conditional again reddens child-session-r2.review.test.ts:745-797, and dating it from the write would redden :579-628.
forget() clears memory before it touches the keychain (child-session.ts:213-214), so a keychain failure cannot leave a dead session's id in memory — the ordering the HUNT5-G-1 fix needed.

No L-006 violation and no unsafe cast in the new SQL: the recovery audit insert passes plain column parameters and no jsonb at all (child-auth.ts:317-320); the row satisfies audit_events' constraints (`actor_kind in (...,'system',...)`, action length 1..100, supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:405-406), and no test asserts an exact audit action list for a family that refreshes, so the new action breaks nothing.

Lock ordering in the recovery cannot deadlock against the ordinary path: the recovery takes the consumed row then its replacement (child-auth.ts:240, :291) while an ordinary rotation locks one row only (child-auth.ts:240), so there is no cycle; and the client's single-flight refresher makes two simultaneous retries of one attempt unreachable.
A-child-refresh.notes:
What I could and could not execute. I ran the mobile suite for my area (`npx vitest run src/family/child-session-r2.review.test.ts` in apps/mobile): 22/22 green, which let me confirm the HUNT5-G-1/G-3 cases behave as their docstrings claim. I could NOT run apps/api/tests/*: those need a local Postgres (pnpm db:local) which is not up in this container, so every claim about mobile-r2.review.test.ts and auth.test.ts is derived by reading the route, the limiter, the harness and the migrations, and by counting requests by hand — not observed. Being read-only I also could not do mutation testing; where I say a mutation would redden a case I derived it from the code path, and I said so.

Three residuals I deliberately did NOT file, so the lead knows they were looked at. (1) The two-minute recovery window re-opens BUG-244 for any retry later than two minutes, including most OS-kill relaunches; child-auth.ts:279-280 states this plainly ("Outside the window, behaviour is exactly the pre-BUG-244 unpairing") and the lead's round-5 decision says "do not re-open it", so it is a documented deferral — only the prose about the keychain mirror (HUNT6-A-3) is filed. (2) `await refreshFinished()` at child-session.ts:276 is now redundant: this diff gave `forget()` the same `pendingRequest = null` (child-session.ts:213) and `unpairChildDevice` already deletes the same key (mode.ts:304), so the line has no observable effect. It is belt-and-braces rather than misleading, so I left it. (3) `unpairChildDevice` (mode.ts:301-305) deletes without a `.catch`, so a momentarily unavailable keychain — the exact failure the new test at child-session-r2.review.test.ts:745 models for setItem — makes `forget()` reject, which makes `refresh()` reject instead of returning null and leaves the refused refresh token in storage; and `signOutClosedAccount` (mode.ts:289-296) ends the child session without going through `forget()`, so the cached child access token and `pendingRequest` survive it in memory. Both are pre-existing and live in mode.ts, which is outside my five files, so they belong to whoever owns that file this round — flagging them here rather than filing so they are not lost the way L-048/L-052 describes.

One thing I could not settle either way: whether "visible to the family" in HUNT6-A-2 is meant to include a parent querying the Supabase Data API directly. The grant and the RLS policy do permit it, so I filed that finding on the narrower ground that no product surface performs the read and the ops signal is info level.

findings.title: HUNT5-B-5 guarantees only ONE newest unresolved row per kind, so a second just-emailed flag is still absent from the only page its email names
findings.requirement: CS-R2-07 / CS-R4-01 / HUNT5-B-5: no unresolved safety report a grown-up must act on is absent from GET /v1/safety-reports, the one surface the flag email points at
findings.mechanism: The fix adds `newest_flag` (privacy.ts:885-892) and `newest_child` (privacy.ts:899-905), each `order by created_at desc limit 1`. So the response is `the 200 OLDEST unresolved rows of the kind` UNION `exactly one row — the single newest`. The comment at privacy.ts:870-871 and the constant doc at privacy.ts:151-158 assert more than that: "Each kind also always contributes its NEWEST unresolved row, so the flag a parent was just emailed about is on the page that email names even behind a full window" and "nothing unresolved is absent from the response except rows in the middle of a drain that is under way". One `safety_flag_email` job is enqueued per report (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:2299-2303, inside `safetyResponse`, which runs once PER QUESTION), and each email says "open Privacy & safety to see the flag and what you can do next: <origin>/app/privacy" (apps/api/src/providers/index.ts:148) with no per-report deep link and no GET /v1/safety-reports/:id anywhere in privacy.ts. So a single scan that flags two answers produces two flags and two emails; with 200 unresolved flags already open, `unresolved_flags` takes the 200 oldest and `newest_flag` returns only the later of the two, and the earlier flag — which a guardian was emailed about — is in no response and reachable from no surface. The same holds for the child branch after HUNT5-B-4 flipped it to `order by created_at asc` (privacy.ts:897): a child who files three disclosures behind a full window has only the newest listed. The second quoted clause is also untrue of the parent branch, whose oldest rows beyond 200 (privacy.ts:906-913, newest-first) are absent with no family-visible drain at all.
findings.repro: In apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts, take the existing HUNT5-B-5 case ('lists a just-filed flag behind a full page of older open flags', line ~940) and add ONE more system flag NEWER than `reportId` (same shape: reporter_kind 'system', category 'severe_risk', status 'escalated', question_id = questionId, transcription_at = flag.transcription_at + interval '1 minute' to satisfy safety_reports_system_once). Total unresolved system rows = 202. Then `GET /v1/safety-reports` as the unlocked parent and assert `reports.map(r => r.id)` contains BOTH `reportId` and the extra id. It contains only the extra one: `unresolved_flags` holds the 200 oldest fillers and `newest_flag` returns the single newest row outside that window. Both ids had a `safety_flag_email` job enqueued.
findings.user_impact: A parent is emailed "a grown-up needs to look at this" and told to open Privacy & safety. The flag is not on that page and there is nowhere else in the product to see it. On a worksheet where the safety screen flags two answers, one of the two flags is invisible until the guardian has resolved enough of the 200 oldest rows to make room — and a child's later disclosures are hidden the same way.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the three things that could already prevent it. (1) The de-dup predicate `id not in (select id from unresolved_flags)` (privacy.ts:889) is not a second row source — the CTE is `limit 1`. (2) No client truncation hides or rescues anything: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:1194 renders `reports?.reports ?? []` in full and apps/mobile/app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:346 maps all rows, so what the API omits is genuinely absent. (3) The existing tests cannot catch it: the HUNT5-B-5 case inserts exactly ONE flag newer than the window and asserts `pendingFlags` has length exactly `UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE + 1`, which is the one-row bound itself; CS-R4-01's fillers are all `reporter_kind='parent'`. BUG-257's ledger row (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:270) has residual '—', and the lead's instruction there was "always include the newest unresolved row of each kind, so the flag the email points the parent at is never absent" — the residual is not recorded anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the second window a bounded PAGE, not one row: for each drainable kind, union the oldest-first drain window with a newest-first window of the same size (`... and id not in (select id from <window>) order by created_at desc limit UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE`). The total stays bounded (at most 2 pages per kind) and no unresolved row of a kind can be absent unless that kind has more than 400 open rows. Rewrite privacy.ts:151-158 and :869-873 to state the bound that is actually true, and say explicitly which rows CAN be absent (the middle of a very long queue) rather than claiming none can.

findings.title: 0890's L-037 sweep stopped at the slot: a Data-API request_deletion leaves the deleted child's finished exports downloadable, while privacy.ts states the withdrawal unconditionally
findings.requirement: spec P4 "Deletion requests should stop processing immediately" / "Purge active uploads, derivatives"; RV-privacy-3, RV-privacy-4; L-037 (the same pre-check on EVERY surface offering the action)
findings.mechanism: Migration 0890 exists because `public.request_deletion` is granted to `authenticated` (0890:104) and the Supabase Data API can call it with a parent's own access token, so effects that lived only in the Hono handler were missing on that surface. The round moved ONE of those effects into the function (the slot release, 0890:86-88) and left the other. `withdrawExports` (privacy.ts:357-395) is still handler-only, invoked at privacy.ts:651 after the RPC transaction, and 0890's body touches child_sessions, child_devices, jobs, assignments, families, family_memberships, child_profiles and child_slot_assignments — never `public.data_exports`. Meanwhile privacy.ts:345 states the property with no qualifier: "a deletion withdraws every finished export file that holds the deleted data as soon as it is requested … The rows become 'expired' (the download route refuses them …) and the files are removed from private storage." The download route has no deletion check at all: apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts:43-49 refuses only on `status !== 'ready'`, a missing storage_path, or `expires_at <= now`. So after a child-scope request_deletion filed through the Data API (which leaves the family live and the caller's membership active, unlike the family scope), GET /v1/exports/:id/download still mints a signed URL for a family_data or progress export containing that child's homework, transcriptions, results and safety-notice rows. The only thing that ends it is the deletion_purge job, which removes the export objects itself (apps/api/src/jobs/dispatcher.ts:266-297) — so the window is until the next job tick in normal operation, and unbounded if that job dead-letters (dispatcher.ts:226-246 keeps re-queueing a successor, which is exactly the dead-letter case FL-R4-01 was written for).
findings.repro: A DB+API case: seed a family with one child, build a `family_data` export to `ready` with a storage_path (the CS-R4-02 harness in privacy-r2.review.test.ts already does this), grant an adult unlock, then call `public.request_deletion(family, child)` through `db.asParent` (the client-role path, exactly as supabase/tests/hardening_r5_db.test.ts:60-66 does) instead of POST /v1/deletion. Assert `select status, storage_path from public.data_exports` — it is still `('ready', <path>)` — and then `GET /v1/exports/<id>/download` with a recently unlocked parent token returns 200 with a signed URL. Via POST /v1/deletion the same assertions give `expired` / null and a 409.
findings.user_impact: A parent asks PencilLift to delete a child's data. On the database surface the product's own threat model treats as live, the finished export file holding that child's homework stays downloadable and is not withdrawn "as soon as it is requested" as the code and the spec commitment say — and if the purge job dead-letters it is never withdrawn at all, while the deletion request sits at 'requested' for ever.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a backstop on each of the three places one could live. (1) The download route: apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts is the whole file — it queries only kind/status/storage_path/expires_at and never reads deletion_requests or child_profiles.status. (2) The database: grep of `data_exports` across supabase/migrations shows no trigger and no statement in any function that expires rows at request time; app.purge_family_data only DELETEs them (0820_support_cases_purge.sql:122), which is the purge, not the request. (3) The export builder's deletion check is for QUEUED exports only (privacy.ts:352-353, 'the builder leaves out every child with an open deletion request'), not for rows already `ready`. BUG-254's ledger row (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:267) records the fix as 'Two halves' — the migration and the API statement — and its residual column is '—'; nothing in docs/Bug_Ledger.md or docs/Lessons_Learned.md records the export withdrawal as a remaining Data-API gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the export withdrawal to `public.request_deletion` in a new migration beside the slot release, as the same kind of backstop: `update public.data_exports set status = 'expired', expires_at = least(coalesce(expires_at, now()), now()) where family_id = p_family and (status = 'ready' or (status = 'expired' and storage_path is not null)) and (p_child is null or child_id = p_child or child_id is null)`. That alone makes export-download.ts refuse it (`status !== 'ready'`), and the storage objects keep being removed by the purge handler and by the handler's own `withdrawExports`, which stays as the file-removing half. Then change privacy.ts:341-355 to say which half is the database's and which is the handler's, instead of asserting the whole property of the handler. Migration numbering is a lead-only registration point (CLAUDE.md), so the number must be assigned by the lead.

findings.title: 0890 takes child_profiles before child_slot_assignments, the reverse of the archive route, so a concurrent archive and child deletion of the same child deadlock
findings.requirement: BUG-106 / FL-R4-02 lock ordering — every writer of a family's rows takes them in one order; BUG-106's recorded sweep states of the 0200 slot-capacity path that "their writers take the family row first or never fire them"
findings.mechanism: The archive route locks in the order families -> child_slot_assignments -> child_profiles: `lockFamily` at apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:511, then the release UPDATE at family.ts:532-533 (row-exclusive on the open assignment row), then `update public.child_profiles set status = 'archived'` at family.ts:535-536 (guarded by `child.status !== 'archived'`, so it does run for an active child). The new statement in 0890 gives `request_deletion` the opposite order and no family lock at all: `update public.child_profiles set status = 'archived'` at 0890:83, then `update public.child_slot_assignments` at 0890:86-88. POST /v1/deletion (apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:595-611) never calls lockFamily either, so the two transactions are not serialised by the families row. Interleave them on one active child C holding slot A: the archive transaction takes the family row, then A; the deletion transaction takes C; the archive transaction then blocks on C and the deletion transaction blocks on A — SQLSTATE 40P01, and Postgres aborts one of them. The migration's own deadlock reasoning at 0890:29-32 considers only `app.enforce_slot_capacity`'s family lock (which is correctly shown to be unreachable because the trigger returns at 0200_billing.sql:118-120 when `new.released_at is not null`); it does not consider the ordering against the route that also writes both rows.
findings.repro: A two-connection test in the style of apps/api/tests/child-auth-hardening.test.ts's lock-order case. Seed an active child with an open slot assignment and one paid slot. Open connection 1: begin, `select 1 from public.families where id = F for update`, then `update public.child_slot_assignments set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'archived' where family_id = F and child_id = C and released_at is null`. Open connection 2 as the parent: begin, `select public.request_deletion(F, C)` — it takes child_profiles C and blocks on A. Back on connection 1: `update public.child_profiles set status = 'archived' where id = C`. One of the two aborts with 40P01. Driving it through the routes instead (POST /v1/children/C/archive and POST /v1/deletion concurrently) makes one of them answer 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE.
findings.user_impact: A guardian who archives a child while the other guardian (or the same parent on a second device) deletes that child's data gets "The service is busy. Please try again." — the same 503 BUG-106 and FL-R4-02 were filed and fixed for. Nothing is written, so a retry succeeds, but a lock-order inversion is a defect this codebase has twice treated as must-fix.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the two guards that could stop it. (1) `visibleChild` (family.ts:92-116, called at family.ts:514) refuses a deletion-pending child, but it runs BEFORE the deletion row exists in this interleaving, so it does not serialise anything — it only closes the case where the deletion committed first. (2) `lockFamily` does not help, because only one side takes it: 0890's child branch never touches public.families (0890:80-89 — the families UPDATE is in the `p_child is null` branch only) and privacy.ts's POST /deletion has no lockFamily call. I also checked that the archive route really reaches the child_profiles UPDATE: it is guarded only by `child.status !== 'archived'` (family.ts:534), true for the active child that holds the slot. BUG-106's residual column records the slot-capacity sweep as clean because "their writers take the family row first"; 0890 added a writer that does not, and neither BUG-253 nor BUG-254 records a lock-order residual.
findings.suggested_fix: Swap the two statements in 0890's child branch so the slot release runs BEFORE `update public.child_profiles` — that gives request_deletion the same assignment-then-child order the archive route uses and removes the cycle without any new lock. (Belt and braces: `perform 1 from public.families where id = p_family for update` at the top of the child branch, which also matches the 'family row first' invariant BUG-106 recorded.) Re-state 0890:29-32 as a claim about lock ORDER against every writer of these two tables, not only against the capacity trigger.

findings.title: SlotReleaseFailed strips every SQLSTATE, including the transient codes app.ts deliberately answers 503 for; the comment and its test assert a lost grant is the release's only plausible failure
findings.requirement: apps/api/src/app.ts:174-184 / errors.ts:100-104 — lock contention the database resolved by aborting the transaction is an expected outcome answered 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After and logged as `db_transient_conflict`, not an unexpected 500
findings.mechanism: `SlotReleaseFailed` (privacy.ts:563-569) keeps the cause only on `.cause`, and the wrapper is applied to EVERY throw out of `releaseChildSlot` (privacy.ts:604-608). `pgErrorCode` reads `.code` off the thrown object and never walks `cause` (apps/api/src/errors.ts:35-37), and `expectedError` (app.ts:174-184) is built on the same helper, so the wrapper does not merely hide 42501 from the handler's own branch — it hides 40P01, 40001 and 55P03 from `isTransientDbError` (errors.ts:101-103) as well. A lock-contention abort raised by the release therefore reaches app.ts:128-133 as an unexpected error: 500 INTERNAL, no Retry-After, and an `unhandled_error` log at level error under the name `SlotReleaseFailed`, instead of 503 with Retry-After: 1 and the `db_transient_conflict` warn. The class doc at privacy.ts:549-561 describes the wrapper's effect as "a generic 500 logged under this class's name, which is what a server-side grant problem is", and the test comment at apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts:850 states outright "The release's only plausible failure mode" — the premise the wrapper rests on is never checked. It is false in the deployment window where the API carries this code but migration 0890 has not been applied yet: the release's predicate then still matches a row, so its UPDATE really does contend for the assignment row with the archive route (see HUNT6-B-3) and can be chosen as the deadlock victim.
findings.repro: Unit-level: in the HUNT5-B-2 test, instead of revoking the grant, make the release's statement raise a transient code — e.g. run a second connection that holds the child's open `child_slot_assignments` row inside a transaction and set `statement_timeout`/`lock_timeout` on the API connection so the release raises 55P03, with migration 0890 not applied (PL_MIGRATIONS_ONLY without 0890) so the predicate still matches. Assert the response is 503 with a Retry-After header and a `db_transient_conflict` log entry. It is 500 INTERNAL with an `unhandled_error` log. The same result follows from throwing a fabricated `{ code: '40P01' }` out of the release.
findings.user_impact: A parent whose deletion request lost a lock race is told "Something went wrong. Please try again." with no Retry-After instead of the product's honest "The service is busy. Please try again.", and operations see an error-level unhandled_error where the codebase intends a warn-level transient. It is the reverse of the mislabelling HUNT5-B-2 set out to fix: one SQLSTATE stopped being read as the wrong thing, and three stopped being read at all.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that the transient path is real and reads `.code` only: `expectedError` calls `isTransientDbError(error)` on the thrown object (app.ts:178) and `isTransientDbError` calls `pgErrorCode` (errors.ts:101), which is `(error as PgErrorLike).code` with no cause walk (errors.ts:35-37). I checked that nothing else restores the classification — app.onError's own `pgErrorCode(thrown)` at app.ts:96 and :115 is the same helper on the same wrapped object. And the new test does not cover it: privacy-r2.review.test.ts:838-874 injects only a missing grant (42501) and asserts `res.status).toBe(500)`, which is precisely the behaviour this finding says is wrong for the other codes. No ledger row records the wrapper's breadth: BUG-254's fix note describes only the 42501 misread.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap selectively, or mark the source instead of erasing it. Cheapest: in the catch at privacy.ts:604-608, re-throw the original error unchanged when `isTransientDbError(error)` (and when `knownConstraintError(error)` matches), wrapping only otherwise. Cleaner: stop wrapping and instead record which statement failed — set a local `let fromRelease = false` before the release and test it in the catch, so the 42501 branch is skipped for a release failure while the error itself keeps its SQLSTATE for app.ts. Then correct privacy.ts:549-561 and the test comment at privacy-r2.review.test.ts:850, which both assert a single possible failure mode.

findings.title: The CS-R4-02 hotline sweep's new key assertion is a tautology over an object literal the test just built, and its comment claims a guard it does not provide
findings.requirement: L-054 (a negative assertion is only as good as the string, range and source it searches); CS-R4-02 — the safety notice's wording never leaves PencilLift in the family_data export
findings.mechanism: `wording` is built two lines earlier as an object literal with exactly three properties (privacy-r2.review.test.ts:814-818), so `expect(Object.keys(wording[0]!)).toEqual(['kind', 'body', 'safety_template_version'])` at :819 asserts the keys of a value the test itself just wrote. No production change can make it red. The comment at :812-813 gives it a purpose it cannot serve: "Naming the fields also means a column added to the export cannot slip into the sweep unnoticed." The only thing that names the export's columns here is the TypeScript annotation at :785-794, which is an unchecked `as` cast over `JSON.parse`, so adding a column to `export-build.ts`'s childFeedback select (apps/api/src/jobs/export-build.ts:520-526) changes neither `data`'s runtime shape checks (there are none) nor `wording`'s keys nor this assertion. The narrow sweep silently keeps searching three fields and nothing tells anyone.
findings.repro: Add a column to the childFeedback select in apps/api/src/jobs/export-build.ts:521 (for example `guard_version as notice_note`) and run `pnpm --filter @pencillift/api run test -- privacy-r2`. Nothing reds: the CS-R4-02 case passes unchanged, including line 819, although the new column is now outside the `/988|422-4453/` sweep. Conversely, deleting line 819 entirely also leaves the suite green, which is the direct demonstration that it cannot fail.
findings.user_impact: No user-visible defect today. The cost is that a fix filed for exactly this class of problem (HUNT5-B-6: two columns silently inside the searched string) shipped a guard that cannot detect the next instance, and a reader of the comment will believe the export's column list is pinned when it is not.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked whether the assertion is redundant-but-harmless rather than misdescribed, and whether the surrounding assertions already cover the stated purpose. The whole-document phrase loop at :780-783 (`expect(body).not.toContain(phrase)` over the entire export text) does catch a full hotline phrase in any new column, so the export property itself is protected — but it uses the two exact phrases, while the narrow sweep uses the looser `/988|422-4453/`, so the narrow sweep is the only check for a partial leak and the one the comment claims is column-proof. I also confirmed the annotation at :785-794 does list exactly the seven columns export-build.ts:521-524 selects today, so the finding is about the assertion's inability to notice a future change, not about a present mismatch. BUG-258's ledger row (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:271) records the fix and names the deterministic re-run; it does not record this assertion as decorative.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the key list from the parsed data instead of from the literal, so it bites: `expect(Object.keys(safetyRows[0]!).filter((k) => !['id', 'question_id', 'child_id', 'created_at'].includes(k))).toEqual(['kind', 'body', 'safety_template_version'])`. A column added to the export then appears in `Object.keys` of a real row and reds the case, which is what the comment claims. If that is not wanted, delete line 819 and the sentence at :812-813 rather than keep prose that asserts a property no assertion holds.

findings.title: The HUNT5-B-7 premise test claims to pin "no surface cancels a deletion request" but searches only the migrations directory and one route file
findings.requirement: L-054 (a negative assertion is only as good as the string, range and SOURCE it searches); the rationale at apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:206-210 is true only while no surface cancels a deletion request
findings.mechanism: The case is titled 'and no surface cancels a deletion request, which is why' (family-hardening-r4.review.test.ts:352) and the docstring at :331-343 presents it as pinning "the premise (no surface cancels a deletion request)". What it actually searches is two narrow sources. (a) `supabase/migrations/*.sql` for the literal lowercase substring `update public.deletion_requests` (:356-364), so a status write spelled `UPDATE public.deletion_requests`, split across a newline after `update`, or done through a variable (`set status = v_status`) is invisible — and app code is not searched at all, although privacy.ts itself writes deletion-adjacent rows from TypeScript. (b) `apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts` only (:369-371), for `r.(delete|patch)('/deletion` and `'/deletion/…cancel`. A cancel endpoint added in any other router — apps/api/src/routes/account.ts (which already owns account closure), support.ts (the owner-admin surface), or family.ts — leaves both assertions green while family.ts:206-210's rationale silently becomes untrue again, which is the exact regression BUG-259 was filed to prevent.
findings.repro: Add, in apps/api/src/routes/account.ts, a handler that does `await deps.db.asService((tx) => tx\`update public.deletion_requests set status = 'cancelled' where id = ${id} and family_id = ${familyId} and status = 'requested'\`)` and register it as `r.post('/account/deletion-cancel', ...)`. Run `pnpm --filter @pencillift/api run test -- family-hardening-r4`. Both HUNT5-B-7 cases pass: the migration scan never reads apps/, and the route regexes only read privacy.ts. The product now cancels deletion requests while the test asserts nothing does.
findings.user_impact: No user-visible defect today. The cost is that the guard the round added against re-introducing the BUG-221 claim (portal copy now says deletion can't be undone from the app) does not cover the places a cancel feature would most plausibly be written, so the same untrue rationale — and then the same untrue parent-facing copy derived from it — can come back green.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that the premise itself currently holds, so this is about the pin and not the code: every `update public.deletion_requests` in the tree sets 'completed' (0620_deletion_purge.sql:232, 0710_jobs_hardening.sql:520, 0820_support_cases_purge.sql:144), and no apps/api source updates that table at all. I checked that the searched sources are genuinely the only ones: `ROOT` is the repo root (resolve(__dirname, '../../..') from apps/api/tests, the same as guard-call-sites.test.ts:13), and the only files opened are supabase/migrations/*.sql and apps/api/src/routes/family.ts and privacy.ts. I also confirmed `expect(updates.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` at :365 protects only against the scan finding nothing in the migrations, not against a cancel written elsewhere. BUG-259's ledger row (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:272) records that the AUTHOR checked privacy.ts, account.ts, family.ts and all migrations by hand — the committed test checks two of those four, and the gap is not recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the source, not the regex: read every `.ts` under apps/api/src (routes and services) plus every migration, normalise whitespace and case, and assert that no statement matching /update\\s+public\\.deletion_requests[^;]*'cancelled'/is exists anywhere and that no route path containing 'deletion' is registered with delete/patch or with a 'cancel' segment in any router file. Keep the existing `updates.length > 0` sanity check so the scan cannot pass by finding nothing.

sweeps_sound: Migration 0890 really is 0840's latest definition plus one statement: I compared supabase/migrations/0890_deletion_slot_release.sql:35-101 against supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:80-141 statement by statement — the gates, the deletion_requests insert, the four revoke/cancel UPDATEs, the family/membership branch, the purge-job insert and the audit insert are byte-identical; nothing was dropped in the regeneration, and no migration after 0890 redefines public.request_deletion (0910_sequence_public_revoke.sql only names it in prose).

The new release cannot flip the deleted child back to a draft: apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts:1079-1086 requires status='active' AND the latest release_reason in ('expired','downgrade'); the deleted child is 'archived' with reason 'archived' (0890:83, :87).

The new release cannot trip the capacity trigger or take its family lock: app.enforce_slot_capacity returns at supabase/migrations/0200_billing.sql:118-120 whenever new.released_at is not null, before `perform 1 from public.families ... for update`, and the trigger is `before insert or update of released_at` (0200_billing.sql:137-139) so it does fire and does return early.

The family.ts:519-529 claim "no path produces archived with an open slot assignment" holds: the only two writers of child_profiles.status='archived' in the tree are apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:535 (which releases the slot at :532 in the same transaction) and 0890:83 (which releases at :86); release_reason 'reassigned' has no producer at all (it appears only in the check constraint at 0200_billing.sql:103), and app.inactivity_delete_family is family-scope only.

newest_flag and newest_child cannot duplicate a row or return one already in the window: `id not in (select id from unresolved_flags/unresolved_child)` runs against a non-null primary key (apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:889, :903), and REPORT_COLUMNS begins with `id` so the subselect resolves (privacy.ts:201).

What the query returns is genuinely rendered: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:1194 and :1272-1275 render every row with no slice, apps/mobile/app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:346 maps all rows, and the final `order by (status <> 'resolved') desc, created_at desc` (privacy.ts:923) puts the newest unresolved row first, so no client truncation hides the newest_flag row.

The HUNT5-B-2 API test can fail and its fixture is honest: service_role in supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:17 is `bypassrls` but NOT superuser, so `revoke update` bites; Postgres checks table privileges at execution rather than per matched row, so the release's UPDATE still raises 42501 although 0890 already made its predicate match nothing; and pgErrorCode (apps/api/src/errors.ts:35-37) plus app.ts:115-119's global 42501→403 branch both read `.code` only, so the wrapper really does keep both from claiming it.

The four supabase/tests/hardening_r5_db.test.ts cases each exercise the real surface: db.asParent sets role 'authenticated' with the parent's claims (supabase/tests/harness.ts run()), the already-released case pins both released_at and release_reason so an unconditional release would red it, and the sibling case drives app.enforce_slot_capacity with a real INSERT rather than asserting a count.

The archive-route regressions at apps/api/tests/family-hardening-r4.review.test.ts:105-118 and :127-139 can both fail: moving the release back inside `if (child.status !== 'archived')` makes the idempotency case report assignedSlots 2, and dropping 'requested' from visibleChild's predicate (family.ts:110-114) makes the 404 case return 200 and free the slot.

findings.title: A renewal invoice's pending proration money is collected and never counted as revenue, while the note, definition, SQL comment and test all say it is counted exactly once
findings.requirement: BILL-R2-4 / HUNT5-C-4 (BUG-263) / L-053 — gross is the money collected
findings.mechanism: mapStripeInvoiceToPeriod (billing-sync.ts:335) returns exactly ONE NormalizedPeriod per invoice, and subscriptionChargeCents books only the subscription line: the primary branch (billing-sync.ts:274) returns that line's own amount net of its own discounts, and the invoice-level fallback (billing-sync.ts:287) subtracts every other proration line. webhooks.ts:314 calls recordBillingPeriod once per invoice.paid, so a renewal invoice that also carries pending proration lines writes ONE billing_periods row whose charged_amount_cents excludes them, and no other row is ever written for that money. loadRevenueMonths (ops-metrics.ts:196-216) sums charged_amount_cents, so the pending proration's net amount appears in no month's gross. This diff's HUNT5-C-4 re-fix asserts the opposite in four new places: the owner-facing note (ops-metrics.ts:159) 'a mid-cycle proration charge is collected money, counted in the month it settles'; REVENUE_DEFINITION (ops-metrics.ts:168) 'a proration charge included ... gross = charged_amount_cents (pre-tax money collected)'; the SQL comment (ops-metrics.ts:207-213) 'The two together are what make the money count exactly once ... and never again inside the renewal that lists it as pending'; and the test comment (apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts:1316) 'whichever way Stripe bills the change, the $10 lands in gross exactly once'. The new test pins the opposite: it records a standalone $10 proration invoice AND a separate renewal invoice carrying its own $10 pending proration line (amount_paid 4999), then asserts end.gross - before.gross === 1000 + 3999 (billing-r2.review.test.ts:1348) — 5999 collected across the two invoices, 4999 in gross. billing-sync.ts:761-763 itself calls this 'the normal shape for a family that added a child, Stripe putting the pending proration item on the next renewal', i.e. Stripe's default create_prorations behaviour, where the real line pair is a negative credit plus a positive charge and the dropped amount is their net.
findings.repro: Post invoice.paid for a renewal: billing_reason 'subscription_cycle', subtotal 4999, tax 0, amount_paid 4999, lines [{period:{start-86400,start}, price:price_family_1, proration:true, amount:1000}, {period:{start,start+30d}, price:price_family_1, amount:3999}]. Then read loadRevenueMonths for that month: stripe gross rises by 3999 although the family paid 4999, and no second billing_periods row exists (select count(*) where provider_period_id like the invoice id → 1). Concretely: change billing-r2.review.test.ts:1348 to expect(end.gross - before.gross).toBe(1000 + 4999) and it is red at 4999.
findings.user_impact: The owner's revenue page understates gross and net by the proration amount on every mid-cycle upgrade that Stripe defers to the next renewal — the default behaviour, and the one this codebase calls normal. That is exactly the loss BUG-263/L-053 was reopened to stop; it was stopped only for the immediately-invoiced proration. Worse, the note printed under the figure tells the owner that money IS counted in the month it settles, so a reconciliation against the Stripe dashboard will not tie out and the owner has no way to see which upgrades are missing.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that nothing else books it: mapStripeInvoiceToPeriod has no loop over lines and recordBillingPeriod is called once per invoice (webhooks.ts:314), so there is no second period row; loadRevenueMonths no longer has any kind filter (ops-metrics.ts:206-213) so the money is not excluded, it is never recorded; the only other revenue surface, recognizedThisMonthCents, reads public.revenue_entries + public.revenue_adjustments (ops-metrics.ts:644), not billing_periods, so it does not compensate. And no test would catch it: the existing BILL-R2-4 case (billing-r2.review.test.ts:481-511) asserts only charged_amount_cents === 3999 for a 5199 invoice and never looks at gross, while the new HUNT5-C-4 case asserts 1000 + 3999 and so locks the defect in.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide which is TRUE (L-053); the money was collected, so record it. In mapStripeInvoiceToPeriod compute the pending proration NET (sum of cents(l.amount) over lines other than the subscription line that are proration === true, which may be negative) and expose it on NormalizedPeriod; in webhooks.ts' invoice.paid branch, when that net is > 0, record a second period with kind 'proration', provider_period_id `${invoice.id}:proration`, charged_amount_cents = net and taxCents = 0 (the unique key (channel, provider_period_id) is text, so no migration is needed). Donation eligibility already filters kind = 'subscription_period' (p17-jobs.ts:274), so the $1 rule is untouched, and the existing refund conversion is untouched because the new row carries no tax. Then update billing-r2.review.test.ts:1348 to 1000 + 4999 and add an assertion that the renewal's own proration lands in gross. If the lead instead decides gross is deliberately subscription-only, all four prose claims must be rewritten to say a pending proration line on a renewal is counted NOWHERE, and the note may not say 'counted in the month it settles'.

findings.title: A won dispute on a taxed charge erases part of an earlier genuine partial refund, contrary to the comment beside it
findings.requirement: BILL-R1-1 / BILL-R4-3 / L-033 (a reversible amount subtracts)
findings.mechanism: After this round a Stripe charge.refunded is written in the CHARGE's unit — converted by charged/(charged+tax) at billing-sync.ts:866-877 — but a Dispute is passed no providerChargeTotalCents (webhooks.ts:368 and :372), so a chargeback and a chargeback_reversed are written at the provider's TAX-INCLUSIVE amount (preTaxRefundCents returns unchanged at billing-sync.ts:793). refunded_cents therefore mixes units. The chargeback branch ADDS and caps: least(charged_amount_cents, refunded_cents + inCharge) (billing-sync.ts:916-919). The reversal branch SUBTRACTS the whole dispute amount: greatest(0, refunded_cents - coalesce(inCharge, charged_amount_cents)) (billing-sync.ts:914, and the same expression decides the settlement at :904). On a taxed charge the sum always exceeds the cap, so the win subtracts more than was ever added. Charge total 4329 (charged 3999, tax 330): a $20 refund stores 1848; a dispute of the remainder 2329 gives least(3999, 1848+2329) = 3999; the dispute is WON with amount 2329 and gives greatest(0, 3999-2329) = 1670, not the 1848 that was genuinely refunded. The comment at billing-sync.ts:885-888 states the opposite: 'with Stripe's dispute `amount` (always present on a Dispute object) an earlier genuine partial refund survives the win as partially_refunded'.
findings.repro: invoice.paid (subtotal 3999, tax 330, amount_paid 4329) → charge.refunded (amount 4329, amount_refunded 2000, refunded false) → charge.dispute.created (amount 2329, charge mapped to the invoice) → charge.dispute.closed status 'won' (amount 2329). Read billing_periods: settlement 'partially_refunded', refunded_cents 1670. It must be 1848. Repeat with tax 0 (charged 4998, total 4998, refund 1000, dispute 3998) and it ends exactly at 1000, which is why the existing case passes.
findings.user_impact: After a dispute the owner wins, the revenue page counts 178 cents of a $20 refund the family really received as kept subscription revenue, and the admin support-case detail shows a refunded figure lower than what was returned. It happens on every taxed charge that saw a partial refund before a dispute that was won; the amount lost is the sales tax on the disputed remainder.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the test that claims to cover this, apps/api/tests/billing-hardening.review.test.ts:381-400 ('a won dispute after a genuine partial refund keeps that refund and does not reinstate the $1'): its fixture is an UNTAXED app_store period (charged 4998, refund 1000, dispute 3998), so 1000 + 3998 hits the cap exactly without exceeding it and the subtraction round-trips; there is no taxed variant of that sequence anywhere in apps/api/tests. I also checked planAdjustment (packages/domain/src/donations/adjustments.ts:117-124): it reinstates only when refundedCents === 0, so the $1 school donation is NOT wrongly reinstated here — the defect is confined to the money figure. And preTaxRefundCents cannot rescue it as written, because the dispute call sites pass providerChargeTotalCents = null by design (webhooks.ts:368, :372) and that null is exactly what disables the conversion (billing-sync.ts:793).
findings.suggested_fix: Put the dispute amount in the charge's unit too. applyRefund already loads the period's tax_amount_cents (billing-sync.ts:845), so a Dispute amount is convertible without any provider total: replace the 'is it tax-inclusive?' inference from providerChargeTotalCents !== null with an explicit amountIsTaxInclusive argument threaded from each call site (true for every Stripe Charge and Dispute figure, false for the RevenueCat path which passes null amounts anyway), and use charged + tax as the denominator for chargeback and chargeback_reversed as well. refunded_cents then holds one unit throughout, so add → cap → subtract round-trips and the comment at billing-sync.ts:885-888 becomes true. Add the taxed variant of the sequence to the BILL-R1-1 tests, and update the owner note at ops-metrics.ts:159, which currently tells the owner a chargeback is recorded 'at its own amount'.

findings.title: A refund that arrived before its invoice is still recorded tax-inclusive, and the reason the docstring gives for that no longer exists
findings.requirement: BILL-R4-3 / HUNT5-C-2 / HUNT5-C-3 / L-037 (the same pre-check on every surface)
findings.mechanism: recordBillingPeriod inserts the period WITH tax_amount_cents (billing-sync.ts:611-620) and then replays a parked refund at billing-sync.ts:640-647 with six arguments, so providerChargeTotalCents takes its null default (billing-sync.ts:832) and preTaxRefundCents returns unconverted at billing-sync.ts:793. The docstring justifies that at billing-sync.ts:821-823: 'A refund parked in `pending_refunds` keeps the provider's figure and is applied with no total, so the cap alone bounds it (that table records no provider total).' That reason was true while the ratio needed the provider total. After HUNT5-C-2 the ratio needs only charged + tax (billing-sync.ts:804-807), and both sit in the row that was just inserted in this same transaction. The guard providerChargeTotalCents === null therefore no longer establishes 'there is nothing to convert with'; it establishes only 'pending_refunds has no column for the total'. The consequence is that the SAME Stripe partial refund is recorded differently depending on webhook arrival order: charge.refunded after invoice.paid → 1848; charge.refunded before invoice.paid → 2000, written against a pre-tax gross of 3999. The note the owner reads (ops-metrics.ts:159) covers only two of the three surfaces — it says the unconverted case is '(a chargeback)' — although the comment directly above it (ops-metrics.ts:151-153) says 'a refund parked before its charge keeps the provider's figure ... The note may not promise one unit for all three.'
findings.repro: With no billing_periods row for in_X yet, post charge.refunded (id ch_1, amount 4329, amount_refunded 2000, refunded false, invoice 'in_X', metadata.billing_ref = the family's ref) — it parks in public.pending_refunds. Then post invoice.paid for in_X (subtotal 3999, tax 330, amount_paid 4329). Read billing_periods: tax_amount_cents 330 and refunded_cents 2000. Post the same two events in the opposite order and refunded_cents is 1848.
findings.user_impact: Whenever Stripe's refund event wins the race with its invoice event, the owner's net revenue for that period is understated by the tax share of the refund (152 cents on a $39.99 charge at 8.25%), and the note beside the column promises the pre-tax unit 'where the provider states the charge total' — which this refund did state. The same refund produces two different recorded figures depending on delivery order.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that the parked path is live and only ever tested with a whole-charge amount: apps/api/tests/billing-hardening.review.test.ts:317-330 parks a 'chargeback' with null, and apps/api/tests/admin-ops.test.ts:198 inserts a pending_refunds row directly; no test parks a PARTIAL refund with an amount and then records a taxed period, so nothing catches it. I also checked pending_refunds' schema (supabase/migrations/0700_billing_integrity.sql:6-14) and it genuinely has no provider-total column, so the docstring's claim about the table is true — it is the inference drawn from it that is now stale. Finally I confirmed the other branch is unaffected: the RevenueCat parked/replayed refund passes refundedCents null (webhooks.ts:514), which short-circuits to the cap and is exact.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop inferring 'convertible' from the presence of a provider total. Preferred (no migration, and it also fixes HUNT6-C-2): replace applyRefund's providerChargeTotalCents parameter with an explicit amountIsTaxInclusive boolean, set true at every Stripe call site (webhooks.ts:348, :368, :372) and at the parked replay for channel 'stripe' (billing-sync.ts:640-647), false for RevenueCat; preTaxRefundCents then converts whenever the flag is set and taxCents > 0. Alternative: a new lead-assigned migration adding provider_total_cents integer to public.pending_refunds, written from chargeTotal in webhooks.ts and passed back at billing-sync.ts:640-647. Either way, widen the owner note at ops-metrics.ts:159 (or drop its '(a chargeback)' parenthesis) so it no longer narrows the unconverted case to a chargeback, which its own comment says it may not do.

findings.title: subscriptionTaxCents' same-tax-rate assumption says it 'is recorded as an open item'; nothing records it, and its unsafe direction has no guard or test
findings.requirement: L-053 (when code and prose disagree, decide which is TRUE)
findings.mechanism: The docstring at billing-sync.ts:313-319 names the one direction of this arithmetic that overstates net revenue — apportioning by pre-tax amount assumes every line carries the same rate, and 'if the subscription line were the exempt one the share would be overstated, which is the unsafe direction' — and closes 'it is recorded as an open item rather than guessed at here'. No such record exists. docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-261's residual column names only the missing invoice tax on the refund path and never differing per-line rates; BUG-263's residual is '—'; docs/Owner_Actions.md has no tax item but #11 (store banking); docs/Release_Readiness.md has none; and docs/ECC_Runs.md:41 lists 'the unstated tax-rate assumption' among the eight observations the lead CLOSED in this round. The only record of the open item is the sentence claiming there is one. The direction is real arithmetic, not hypothetical: with 100 cents of tax levied on a 1000 add-on line beside a 3999 line that is exempt, subscriptionTaxCents (billing-sync.ts:327-331) stores floor(100*3999/4999) = 79 although the tax on this charge is 0, and preTaxRefundCents then shrinks every partial refund of that charge by 79/4078 of itself (billing-sync.ts:804-807).
findings.repro: grep -rn "tax rate|per-line tax|same tax rate" docs/ returns only the BUG-261 row, which does not mention differing per-line rates — a reader following the docstring to the records finds the item closed, not open. For the arithmetic half: mapStripeInvoiceToPeriod on an invoice with tax 100, lines [{period,price,amount:3999},{period,price:other,amount:1000}] stores tax_amount_cents 79; a charge.refunded of 2000 on a charge total of 5099 then records 1962 instead of 2000.
findings.user_impact: The only branch of the refund conversion that can make clawed-back money look like kept revenue has no owner, no test and no entry in the records the lead reads on resume, so it will not be revisited when per-line tax is added to the StripeInvoice shape — and a later reader who follows the comment will conclude it is already tracked.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I searched the four record files CLAUDE.md names for this (docs/Bug_Ledger.md, docs/Owner_Actions.md, docs/Release_Readiness.md, docs/Lessons_Learned.md L-050..L-054) and none carries a per-line-tax-rate item; ECC_Runs.md:41 records it as closed. I also confirmed no code path fails safe on it: subscriptionTaxCents (billing-sync.ts:321-332) never compares the invoice's tax against a plausible single rate — it only guards tax === 0, chargedCents <= 0 and otherLinesCents <= 0 — and no test in apps/api/tests builds an invoice whose lines would carry different rates.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the residual to docs/Bug_Ledger.md under BUG-261 (or as a new row), naming the exempt-subscription-line case, its direction (net revenue overstated, i.e. the unsafe one) and what closes it: model Stripe's per-line tax (lines.data[].tax_amounts) in StripeInvoice and use the subscription line's own tax instead of the ratio. Until that lands, either soften the docstring to state plainly that it is NOT recorded anywhere, or make subscriptionTaxCents fail safe by returning 0 when the invoice's tax is not within a cent of one common rate applied to charged + otherLinesCents (0 is the documented no-op, which can only over-record a refund).

sweeps_sound: preTaxRefundCents stays in integer cents and can never exceed the charge — apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts:804-807: Math.round over an integer product and integer divisor, wrapped in Math.min(chargedCents, …); at the approved prices the product (≈7000 × 7000) is far inside the safe-integer range and no float rate is ever formed.

The apportionment is a no-op on a single-line taxed renewal, so the existing BILL-R4-3 number is unchanged — billing-sync.ts:327-330 returns the WHOLE tax when otherLinesCents <= 0, making charged + tax === amount_paid (3999 + 330 = 4329) exactly the old Charge-total denominator; apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts:1066-1071 still reads 1848.

subscriptionTaxCents floors and clamps, so an ordinary extra line can only shrink the stored tax — billing-sync.ts:327-331. I tried a discounted subscription line, a heavily discounted other line, a missing line.amount and a negative (credit) proration line clamped to 0, and could not drive the stored tax above the tax really on the charge by any of them; only differing per-line rates do, which is HUNT6-C-4.

taxCents is always an integer ≥ 0 before it reaches Postgres — billing-sync.ts:322 (Math.max(0, cents(invoice.tax) ?? 0)), :331 (Math.floor), the literal 0 for RevenueCat at billing-sync.ts:117, and the column's own named check at supabase/migrations/0900_billing_period_tax.sql:35-37.

A period recorded before migration 0900 really is an exact no-op and not a wrong number — the column defaults to 0 (0900:30-31), preTaxRefundCents short-circuits on taxCents <= 0 (billing-sync.ts:797), and supabase/tests/billing_tax.test.ts:93-110 proves the default on a row inserted without naming the column.

The new column inherits 0200's grants rather than acquiring any of its own — the revokes at supabase/migrations/0200_billing.sql:295-302 are table-level (insert/update/delete from authenticated, all from anon), and the shim's `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on tables` (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:107) applies to newly created TABLES only, never to a new column of an existing one, so no column-level privilege appears for authenticated, anon or pl_child.

The DB test's role cases are not running as the one role its migration failed to revoke (the L-054 trap) — pl_child holds no grant at all on public.billing_periods (its only public grants are supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:525-527) and anon was revoked at 0200:295, so both 'permission denied' assertions bite (supabase/tests/billing_tax.test.ts:150-160); and the parent-write case at :162-173 asserts 'permission denied' rather than a zero-row update, which tests the grant and not RLS.

The new negative assertion about the note does bite — apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts:1355 /proration[^.]*never revenue/ does match the pre-fix note string (there is no '.' between 'proration' and 'never revenue' in it), and the paired positive assertions at :1356-1358 pin the true copy, so no rewrite can satisfy both at once.

Both owner-facing strings fit the contract's caps and the test proves it against the contract, not a copied number — the note is 398 of 400 and the definition 578 of 600 (packages/contracts/src/admin-ops.ts:167 and :43), parsed at billing-r2.review.test.ts:1364-1365.

The revenue query's new multi-line SQL comment cannot break the statement — the apostrophes inside it (owner's) sit in `--` comments, which Postgres' lexer treats as whitespace to end of line, and the comment block (ops-metrics.ts:207-213) carries no ${} placeholder, so nothing is interpolated into it.

The invoice.paid replay is still idempotent with the new column — on conflict (channel, provider_period_id) do update (billing-sync.ts:619-623) writes no second row and leaves settled_at alone, and billing-r2.review.test.ts:1307-1311 counts exactly one row after a second delivery under a fresh event id.

Putting kind 'proration' back into gross cannot touch the $1 school donation — the accrual query filters p.kind = 'subscription_period' (apps/api/src/services/p17-jobs.ts:274), so a proration period can neither earn nor lose an accrual, and full-refund reversal still fires for any partial refund (packages/domain/src/donations/adjustments.ts:110-116).

tax_amount_cents never leaks into a figure anyone reads as revenue — the only read in production is billing-sync.ts:845 inside applyRefund; loadRevenueMonths (ops-metrics.ts:196-216), support.ts:185/:213 and admin-ops.ts:324 all select explicit column lists that exclude it, and no `select *` on billing_periods exists in apps/api/src or packages.

The BILL-R4-4 credit-balance case still converts exactly — subscriptionChargeCents caps charged at amount_paid − tax (billing-sync.ts:265-270), so charged + tax equals the Charge total and the new denominator matches the provider's own figure to the cent; I could not construct a credit-balance invoice where the conversion moved by more than the documented flooring cent.

findings.title: BUG-264's fix rewrote one of the three places that promise the trailing entitlement sweep a slice; TICK_TRAILING_RESERVE_MS's own docstring still promises it, and the new regression test's search range structurally cannot see it
