findings.mechanism: The call-site comment was rewritten to say the reserve is 'the whole guarantee' and that a long pre-ledger step 'still leaves this step nothing' (dispatcher.ts:1317-1323). The reserve does not give the sweep two minutes: `remaining = TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS - TICK_TRAILING_RESERVE_MS - elapsed` at dispatcher.ts:739 is measured from the TICK's start, so if the twelve pre-ledger steps (dispatcher.ts:1228-1308) burn 14 of the 15 minutes, `remaining` is negative, the ledger claims nothing, and the sweep starts at minute 14 with under a minute — starved by the steps in front of it. The new test cannot catch this: apps/api/tests/jobs-r2.review.test.ts:403-409 slices the source between `const jobs = await step('jobs'` and `const entitlementsReconciled = await step(` and only runs `not.toMatch(/always gets a slice/)` inside that window, which begins 1,216 lines after the sentence that still makes the promise. findings.user_impact: Nobody's screen changes, but the next engineer who sees `entitlementsReconciled: 0` on a tick reads the constant's docstring, concludes the sweep is guaranteed time, and looks for the wrong bug — while the real consequence stands: a family whose subscription lapsed without a webhook keeps paid AI until a lighter tick sweeps them. findings.title: The rewritten docstring in run-truncation.test.ts names the wrong figure and then claims it is inside extraction's cap 'whatever that cap is set to'

findings.title: The new sequence-revoke case's own premise assertion is blind to a PUBLIC grant — the exact defect this same commit fixed in the sibling file
findings.mechanism: The new case added for BUG-265 states its premise at supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1058-1060 — "Premise of the case: the revoke really happened, so nothing below passes because the role still holds USAGE" — and establishes it with `expect(await sequenceGrants()).toEqual([])`. `sequenceGrants` (supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1051-1057) filters `aclexplode(c.relacl)` with `pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) in ('anon','authenticated','pl_child')`. aclexplode reports a grant to PUBLIC with grantee = 0 and `pg_get_userbyid(0)` returns the literal string 'unknown (OID=0)', so a PUBLIC aclitem (`=rwU/postgres`) is filtered out — while `authenticated` holds USAGE and UPDATE through it. That is word for word the defect the round-5 hunt filed as HUNT5-D-3 / BUG-267 against the sibling query in supabase/tests/schema_invariants.test.ts, and which THIS SAME COMMIT fixed there (schema_invariants.test.ts:256-261 now renders grantee 0 as 'PUBLIC' and matches `a.grantee = 0 or ...`). The new query in the other file was written without that fix: right in one place, wrong in the sibling case. It is not a cosmetic duplicate — this query is the case's stated premise, and the whole point of the round's OTHER change here (migration 0910) is that a PUBLIC sequence grant is the live residual of HR4-0860-01.
findings.repro: Verified in a scratch database with the shim + all migrations applied (psql, not a file edit). `grant all on sequence public.audit_events_id_seq to public;` then run the verbatim helper from hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1051-1057: it returns 0 rows, so the premise assertion at :1060 passes. In the same state `has_sequence_privilege('anon'|'authenticated'|'pl_child','public.audit_events_id_seq','USAGE')` and `...,'UPDATE')` are all true, and `pg_get_userbyid(0)` = 'unknown (OID=0)'. The insert at :1064-1074 then succeeds for a reason the case explicitly means to have excluded, and the whole case stays green. As a test: insert `await db.sql`grant all on sequence public.audit_events_id_seq to public`` immediately before line 1060 (revoking it in a finally) and assert the premise goes red — it does not. Run the same plant against schema_invariants.test.ts:253-262's helper and it DOES report `{sequence_name:'audit_events_id_seq', grantee:'PUBLIC', ...}`.
findings.user_impact: Nobody is harmed today — no sequence in public carries a PUBLIC aclitem. The cost is that the one case the round added to prove "an identity insert needs no sequence privilege" can pass because the role under test still holds USAGE through PUBLIC, which is the precise state migration 0910 was added in the same commit to prevent. If that state ever arises (a hosted platform default, a future `grant ... to public`), this case reports the revoke as proven while the ledger sequences are client-writable — one `setval('public.audit_events_id_seq',1,false)` as `authenticated` then breaks every later append to the audit ledger (create_family, request_deletion / spec P4 "delete my data", pairing, activation, consent) until an operator repairs the sequence.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the guard that would prevent it and it is in the other file, not this one: schema_invariants.test.ts:253-262 handles grantee 0, and hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1051-1057 does not. They run against separate databases (supabase/tests/harness.ts:96-111 creates one per test file), so the schema_invariants fix does not cover this case's premise. I also confirmed the whole file is green today (`npx vitest run tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts` → 36/36) so nothing else reddens first, and I confirmed by direct probe that the query really does return zero rows with the PUBLIC grant in place — the blindness is not hypothetical. BUG-265's ledger row and its residual note (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:278) do not record it.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `sequenceGrants` the same shape the sibling now has: `case when a.grantee = 0 then 'PUBLIC' else pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) end as grantee` in the select list and `and (a.grantee = 0 or pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) in ('anon','authenticated','pl_child'))` in the predicate. Better still for a premise about what the role can DO, add `expect(await effectiveSequencePrivilege('authenticated','public.audit_events_id_seq'))` using `has_sequence_privilege`, which accounts for PUBLIC and for role membership without any grantee list at all.

findings.title: 0910's default-privileges revoke is per-schema, so it cannot cancel a GLOBAL PUBLIC default — the migration claims "a sequence created later inherits none", and neither the new test nor the CI invariant can see the global form
findings.mechanism: supabase/migrations/0910_sequence_public_revoke.sql:38 is `alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on sequences from public;` and the header asserts at :16-18 "the deployed schema holds no PUBLIC privilege on any sequence in public, and a sequence created later inherits none" and at :22 "it cancels the schema default so new sequences do not receive it again". Per-schema default privileges are merged ADDITIVELY onto the global/hard-wired default (PostgreSQL `get_user_default_acl` → `aclmerge`), so a per-schema REVOKE can only remove entries from the per-schema `pg_default_acl` row; it cannot subtract a PUBLIC entry held in the GLOBAL row (defaclnamespace = 0). This project already wrote that rule down for functions and used the global form because of it: supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:535-537 says "Per-schema default privileges can only ADD to the global defaults, so the PUBLIC revoke must be global" and 0001:539 is `alter default privileges revoke execute on functions from public;`. 0910 re-opens that lesson for sequences. Two checks that should catch it cannot: the new assertion at supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1215-1220 (`revokedNewSequence`) only ever plants the per-schema form at :1167, and the standing invariant at supabase/tests/schema_invariants.test.ts:283-287 joins `pg_namespace n on n.oid = d.defaclnamespace where n.nspname = 'public'`, which discards the global row whose defaclnamespace is 0.
findings.repro: Ran it in a scratch database with the shim + all 37 migrations applied. `alter default privileges grant all on sequences to public;` (global — no `in schema`). schema_invariants' clientDefaults query (schema_invariants.test.ts:283-289) then returns only `service_role=rwU/postgres` — no offender, invariant green. Re-apply 0910's two statements verbatim. Then `create table public.probe_after (id bigint generated always as identity primary key);` → `pg_class.relacl` for probe_after_id_seq is `{=rwU/postgres,postgres=rwU/postgres,service_role=rwU/postgres}`; `has_sequence_privilege('anon'|'authenticated'|'pl_child','public.probe_after_id_seq','USAGE'/'UPDATE')` are all true; and `set local role authenticated; select setval('public.probe_after_id_seq', 1, false);` returns 1. As a test: in hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1167 plant `alter default privileges grant all on sequences to public` (global) instead of / in addition to the per-schema form — the `revokedNewSequence` expectation at :1215 goes red.
findings.user_impact: If the hosted project carries a global PUBLIC default on sequences (set by the platform before the schema was deployed, or by any future `alter default privileges` without `in schema`), then every sequence created by a migration AFTER 0910 is writable by every role, including `authenticated`. One `setval()` on such a ledger's identity sequence as `authenticated` makes every later append fail on the primary key until an operator repairs the sequence — for audit_events that stops create_family, request_deletion (spec P4 "delete my data"), device pairing, activation and consent; for ai_usage_events it stops settleSpend's cost insert, so the spend hold keeps the owner's AI budget locked to the end of the month. CI stays green throughout, because the shim only ever sets the per-schema form (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:108) and the one invariant that would report a global default filters it out by namespace.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the three things that could already prevent it. (1) 0910:34's blanket `revoke all on all sequences in schema public from public` cleans only sequences that exist when it runs — it does nothing for one created by a later migration. (2) schema_invariants.test.ts:238-274 (the sequence-ACL invariant) does catch such a sequence once it exists — but only in CI, and in CI no global PUBLIC default exists, so it never fires; I confirmed by probe that this invariant's sibling, the default-privileges case at :277-301, returns nothing at all in the planted state. (3) PostgreSQL's hard-wired default for sequences grants nothing to PUBLIC, so the exposure requires an explicit ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES — which is exactly the scenario 0910:4-7 names ("a hosted platform whose schema default names PUBLIC"), and the global spelling of it is not covered. The residual recorded for BUG-267 (docs/Bug_Ledger.md:281, cell 8) is only "the third clause is a migration change and migrations are carved out of my brief" — it does not record that the migration finally written covers only the per-schema form.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the global spelling beside the per-schema one, exactly as 0001:539 does for functions: `alter default privileges revoke all on sequences from public;` (no `in schema`), and correct the prose at 0910:16-22 to say which form each statement cancels. Then close the CI hole: in both default-privileges invariants (schema_invariants.test.ts:210-220 and :281-290) match global rows too — replace the inner join with `left join pg_namespace n on n.oid = d.defaclnamespace where (n.nspname = 'public' or d.defaclnamespace = 0)` — and add a plant of the global form so the widened query is pinned. Finally, plant the global form in hardening_r2_db.test.ts's 0910 case so `revokedNewSequence` covers the branch its name claims.

findings.title: 0910 claims its revoke removes a PUBLIC privilege "wherever it is held now, including a grant made by ... the hosted platform"; a REVOKE by a role that is not the grantor is a silent no-op
findings.mechanism: supabase/migrations/0910_sequence_public_revoke.sql:20-22 states "What a revoke does and does not do, stated plainly: it removes the privilege wherever it is held now, including a grant made by an earlier migration or by the hosted platform before this schema was deployed". PostgreSQL REVOKE removes only privileges granted by the executing role or by roles it is a member of. On hosted Supabase migrations run as `postgres`, which is not a superuser; a PUBLIC grant whose grantor is a platform role (rendered in relacl as `=wU/<grantor>`) is untouched by `revoke all on all sequences in schema public from public` at :34, and the statement reports success with no error — so the migration file commits and the deploy looks clean while the privilege is still held. That is precisely the scenario the sentence names as covered.
findings.repro: Ran it in a scratch database. `create role own1 nosuperuser; create role gr1 nosuperuser; create schema s1 authorization own1;` then as own1: `create sequence s1.q1; grant all on sequence s1.q1 to gr1 with grant option;` then as gr1: `grant usage, update on sequence s1.q1 to public;` → relacl `{own1=rwU/own1,gr1=r*w*U*/own1,=wU/gr1}`. Now as own1 (the object's owner, the role a migration runs as): `revoke all on all sequences in schema s1 from public;` → the statement succeeds, emits nothing, and relacl is byte-for-byte unchanged; `has_sequence_privilege('<any role>','s1.q1','USAGE')` is still true. As a DB test: build the same three-role fixture in supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts, apply 0910's text as the sequence owner rather than as the cluster superuser, and assert `publicSequenceAcl` is empty — it is not.
findings.user_impact: On the owner's hosted project the hardening statement can silently not happen. Nothing is worse than before 0910, but the migration and its record assert a property the deploy does not have, so an operator reading 0910 (or the Release Readiness record that leans on it) will believe the ledger sequences are protected from PUBLIC when they may not be — and the failure mode if they are not is the audit/AI-cost ledger DoS described in the same header at 0910:8-13.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked whether the test suite covers it: the new case at supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1113-1232 applies 0910's text through `db.sql`, which is the harness's superuser connection (supabase/tests/harness.ts:108, `postgres://postgres:...`), and a superuser can revoke anything — so the case can never exercise the non-grantor path. I also checked that PostgreSQL does not fail loudly here: my probe produced no ERROR and no WARNING, just `REVOKE`. And the migration does not hedge — :20-22 asserts the opposite in so many words. Not recorded in docs/Bug_Ledger.md (BUG-267's residual mentions only 0870's revoke lists) or in docs/Lessons_Learned.md L-050..L-054.
findings.suggested_fix: Either narrow the prose at 0910:20-22 to what a revoke by the migration role actually does, or make the migration prove its own post-condition and fail the deploy otherwise — e.g. after :34, `do $$ begin if exists (select 1 from pg_class c, aclexplode(c.relacl) a where c.relkind='S' and c.relnamespace='public'::regnamespace and a.grantee = 0) then raise exception 'PUBLIC still holds a sequence privilege in public; revoke it as the grantor'; end if; end $$;` (which also converts the CI-only invariant into a deploy-time gate). If it is left to an operator, add the step and the diagnostic query to docs/Deployment_Runbook.md and docs/Owner_Actions.md.

findings.title: "No arm of the query above can be dropped and stay green" is false: the pl_child × table-level cell — the original purpose of the invariant — has no plant
findings.mechanism: supabase/tests/schema_invariants.test.ts:106-107 claims "One plant per way a write reaches pl_child, so no arm of the query above can be dropped and stay green", and :144-148 enumerates "the fourth combination". The four plants are PUBLIC+table INSERT (:110), PUBLIC+table DELETE (:122), pl_child+column UPDATE (:134) and PUBLIC+column UPDATE (:149). Over the 2x2 matrix {PUBLIC, pl_child} x {table, column} that is PUBLIC+table twice and the pl_child+table cell not at all. `information_schema.role_column_grants` expands a TABLE-level INSERT/UPDATE grant to every column, so plant 3 is caught by the column arm alone; nothing forces `'pl_child'` to stay in the table-level arm's grantee list at :95. Removing it leaves all four assertions green while `grant delete on public.audit_events to pl_child` or `grant truncate ... to pl_child` — table-only privileges, and the case that the pre-diff query (`grantee = 'pl_child'`, table level, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE) existed to catch — becomes invisible to `childWriteGrants()`.
findings.repro: Ran it against the shim + all migrations. Mutate the table arm at schema_invariants.test.ts:95 from `grantee in ('pl_child','PUBLIC')` to `grantee in ('PUBLIC')`, leaving the column arm untouched. All four plants still return exactly the single expected row: plant 1 → `audit_events|PUBLIC|INSERT`, plant 2 → `audit_events|PUBLIC|DELETE`, plant 3 → `audit_events|pl_child|UPDATE` (via the column arm), plant 4 → `audit_events|PUBLIC|UPDATE`; and the baseline is still empty, so the case stays green. In the same mutated state `grant delete on public.audit_events to pl_child;` produces zero rows from the query while `has_table_privilege('pl_child','public.audit_events','DELETE')` is true. A fifth plant — `grant delete on public.audit_events to pl_child` expecting `{audit_events, pl_child, DELETE}` — turns the mutation red.
findings.user_impact: No live hole: the unmutated invariant does catch a table-level DELETE or TRUNCATE granted to pl_child today. The defect is that the case's own completeness claim is untrue, so the arm that protects children's family rows from a direct client DELETE is the one arm no plant proves, and a future edit that narrows it passes CI — after which a slip like `grant delete on public.<family table> to pl_child` (or a re-exposed schema default) would let a paired child's session delete family rows behind RLS with nothing in CI to say so.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked whether another case covers the pl_child table-level cell and none does: '[DB-R2-04] no client role holds TRUNCATE, TRIGGER or REFERENCES' (schema_invariants.test.ts:160-200) covers TRUNCATE for pl_child but not DELETE/INSERT/UPDATE, and its only plant is a column-level REFERENCES to `authenticated`. I confirmed with psql that the column arm really does report a table-level grant expanded per column (so plant 3 does not pin the table arm), and that the whole file is green today (`npx vitest run tests/schema_invariants.test.ts` → 10/10), so the mutation is genuinely silent. Not in docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-248..BUG-293 (BUG-267 is the sequence query, not this one) and not covered by L-054's recorded instances.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing plant next to the other four: `await db.sql`grant delete on public.audit_events to pl_child`` expecting `[{ table_name: 'audit_events', grantee: 'pl_child', privilege_type: 'DELETE' }]`, revoked in `finally`, then re-assert empty. That pins `'pl_child'` into the table-level arm, which no existing plant does. Then correct the comment at :106-107 and :144-148 to name the 2x2 matrix honestly (PUBLIC/pl_child x table/column), since it currently describes three cells as four.

findings.title: 0910 says hardening_r2_db.test.ts "pins both facts"; the case pins neither as stated — idempotency is checked only on pg_default_acl, and "0870 unchanged" is one toContain
findings.mechanism: supabase/migrations/0910_sequence_public_revoke.sql:26-28 asserts "0870 is left exactly as it shipped; this is an additive second pass over the same objects with the same two statement shapes, and applying it twice is a no-op (supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts pins both facts)." The case named for that, supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1234 'is idempotent, and 0870 is left exactly as it was', does two things. (a) It snapshots `pg_default_acl` for `defaclobjtype = 'S'` in schema public before and after re-applying 0910 (:1242-1256) — i.e. only the object the SECOND statement touches. The first statement at 0910:34 acts on `pg_class.relacl` of every sequence in public, and no relacl snapshot is taken, so the idempotency of the statement that does the actual revoking is unasserted. (b) It checks `expect(text0870).toContain('revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon, authenticated, pl_child;')` (:1262-1264). That is one line of 0870; 0870:49 — the second of the two statement shapes 0910:26-27 says it mirrors — is not pinned at all, and any addition to 0870 keeps the assertion green. So the assertion cannot fail for the property in its own name.
findings.repro: Delete supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:49 (`alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon, authenticated;`) and run `npx vitest run tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts`: the case 'is idempotent, and 0870 is left exactly as it was' is still green, although 0870 is no longer as it shipped and 0910's "additive second pass over the same objects with the same two statement shapes" premise no longer holds. (A different file, schema_invariants.test.ts:277-301, does go red — which is the point: this case does not pin what its name and 0910:28 say it pins.) For half (a): the test never selects `relacl`, so no mutation of the first statement's effect can redden it.
findings.user_impact: Records only — no user-visible behaviour. The cost is that a reader of 0910 is told a test guarantees two properties that it does not, which is how the two previous rounds shipped fixes that did not work: the next person deciding whether 0910 may be re-run, or whether 0870 may be edited, will trust a green case that is insensitive to both questions.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked what else could pin the two facts. For "0870 unchanged": nothing else in the repo asserts on 0870's text (`grep -rn 0870_hardening_r4_db` finds only docs/Bug_Ledger.md prose and this one assertion). For "applying twice is a no-op": no test snapshots sequence relacl across a re-application — the only relacl queries in the new block (`publicSequenceAcl`, hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1090-1094) run inside the rolled-back transaction of the OTHER case and are never compared across two applications. findings.title: The refused-sign-out notice tells the parent to "sign out on your phone", which cannot end the session the server was never told about
findings.mechanism: SignOutControl.tsx:15-16 defines the copy the WEBR5-E-2 fix now shows on the refused-but-cleared path: "This computer is signed out. We could not tell PencilLift's servers to end the session, so sign out on your phone, or change your password if you are worried." It is navigated into /sign-in state at SignOutControl.tsx:92 and rendered at apps/web/src/pages/auth/SignInPage.tsx:45-49. The only remedy the sentence names first — signing out on the phone — cannot touch the session in question. Every sign-out in this product is scope 'local' by design (L-039): the portal adapter defaults to it at apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:351, and the phone's sign-out is hard-coded to it at apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:112, whose own comment says "Ends the session on THIS device only" and whose control is labelled "Sign out of the parent account on this device" (apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:495). GoTrue's /logout?scope=local revokes only the calling session, so the phone's sign-out revokes the phone's refresh token and leaves the web session's row untouched. There is no "sign out everywhere" anywhere in the product: `SignOutScope`'s 'global' member (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:71) has no caller (grep for `'global'` across apps/web/src finds only comments and an unrelated monetization key), and the only revoke endpoint, POST /v1/devices/:id/revoke, ends CHILD device sessions (apps/web/src/pages/app/DevicesPage.tsx:114). So of the two remedies offered, the first does nothing and only the second (a password change) can work. The path is not exotic: with a fresh access token and no network, auth-js 2.116.0 removes the local session and returns the fetch error (node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.116.0/.../dist/main/GoTrueClient.js:3435-3445), so the adapter reports `serverNotTold: true` (supabase-auth.ts:372-374) and every offline press of Sign out lands the parent on this notice.
findings.repro: In apps/web/src/App.signout.test.tsx, extend the WEBR5-E-2 test ('leaves the portal for the sign-in page when the refusal cleared this browser's session'): after `const notice = await screen.findByRole('alert')`, assert `expect(notice.textContent).not.toMatch(/on your phone/i)` and instead assert the notice names an action that can actually end the server-side session. It goes red today, because SignOutControl.tsx:16 says "sign out on your phone" and App.signout.test.tsx:245 currently pins that exact phrase. The behavioural repro a person meets: sign in to the portal, go offline (or block the auth host), press Sign out; the browser session is removed and the parent is told to sign out on their phone — do that, come back online, and the web session's refresh token is still valid server-side.
findings.user_impact: A parent on a shared family, school or library computer whose sign-out did not reach the servers is given a first instruction that does nothing. They sign out on their phone, believe the session on the shared computer is now closed everywhere, and skip the one remedy (changing the password) that can actually end it. The same sentence, word for word, is also shown on the account-closure path (apps/web/src/pages/public/AccountDeletionPage.tsx:48-49), where the parent has even more reason to believe they have closed everything.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a global sign-out before filing. `grep -rn "'global'" apps/web/src` returns only the type member at apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:71 and three comments — no call site passes it, and SignOutControl.tsx:76 passes 'local'. `grep -rn "scope" apps/mobile/src` returns only apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:112 `signOut({ scope: 'local' })`. The API has no parent-session revocation route (the revoke endpoints in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:596 and child-auth.ts:384 act on public.child_sessions). I also read auth-js's _signOut (GoTrueClient.js:3422-3453) to confirm the local scope is what is sent. No guard, branch or test corrects the copy: App.signout.test.tsx:245 and apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1266 both assert the phrase is present, so the suite currently locks the wrong advice in. The BUG-270 and BUG-280 ledger entries record the copy as the fix; neither records the phone clause as a known-useless residual.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the phone clause and name a remedy that works. Something like: "This computer is signed out. We could not tell PencilLift's servers to end the session, so change your password to end it everywhere — signing out on your phone only ends the session on that phone." Keep the two copies byte-identical (SignOutControl and AccountDeletionPage), and change both tests to assert the new constant rather than a paraphrase (L-054). If the owner wants the honest remedy to exist, the alternative is to add a real "Sign out everywhere" action (scope 'global' already exists in the type) and point the notice at it; that is a product decision for the lead.
findings.requirement: WEB-R2-01 / WEB-R4-AUTH-2 / L-039

findings.title: assuranceLevel()'s new guard checks the response wrapper, not the field that carries the level, so an unreadable level is still returned as 'aal1'
findings.mechanism: This diff added `|| !data` at supabase-auth.ts:310 and the claim at supabase-auth.ts:307 — "`null` only when the level could not be read at all — never as a stand-in for aal1" — repeated in the interface doc at apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:56-59 ("`null` is never 'aal1', so a caller deciding whether an owner has to re-prove a factor must refuse"). But auth-js does not signal an unreadable level through `data`; it signals it through `data.currentLevel === null` with `error: null`. GoTrueClient.js:5074-5078 returns `{ data: { currentLevel: null, nextLevel: null, currentAuthenticationMethods: [] }, error: null }` when there is no session, and :5080-5083 leaves `currentLevel` null whenever the access token carries no `aal` claim. Line 311 then collapses that to `'aal1'`: `data.currentLevel === 'aal2' ? 'aal2' : 'aal1'`. So the one value that means "I could not read the level" is spent as the answer the comments say it must never be — the same mistake shape WEBR5-E-1 was raised to fix for the factor list, left in place for the level beside it. Downstream, apps/web/src/pages/app/PinResetPage.tsx:76-79 refuses only on `level === null`, so an unreadable level reported as 'aal1' takes the `not_needed` branch and PinResetPage.tsx:118 runs the session-replacing password grant with no two-step step.
findings.repro: A unit test on the real adapter over a labeled fake client (the shape apps/web/src/pages/admin/MfaPage.test.tsx already builds): `getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel: () => Promise.resolve({ data: { currentLevel: null, nextLevel: null, currentAuthenticationMethods: [] }, error: null })`. Assert `await adapter.account!.assuranceLevel()` is `null` — it resolves `'aal1'` today. Then the page-level half: same fake plus `listFactors: () => Promise.resolve({ data: { totp: [{ id: 'synthetic-factor', status: 'verified' }] }, error: null })`, render PinResetPage and run `confirmPassword()`; assert an alert matching /two-step verification/i and `expect(signInWithPassword).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. Today the page goes straight to the PIN step and the grant runs.
findings.user_impact: Narrow, but in the same direction as the bug this round was fixing: on a session whose access token carries no `aal` claim (a project with a custom access-token hook that reshapes claims, or a token minted before `aal` was standard), an owner who resets their parent PIN is read as aal1 and is not asked for their authenticator code, so the password grant replaces their session with no re-verification. Mainly, the two comments this diff added assert a property the adapter does not have, and a later reader hardening the next caller will trust them.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I read the shipped auth-js 2.116.0 rather than relying on memory: node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.116.0/node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/main/GoTrueClient.js:5070-5091 is the no-jwt branch, and it returns `error: null` with `currentLevel: null` in both the no-session and the no-`aal`-claim cases. No guard downstream covers it: PinResetPage.tsx:76 tests `level === null` only, and MfaPage.tsx:41 tests `aal === null` only — neither can see `currentLevel`. The MfaPage tests added in this diff use `AAL1_OK = { data: { currentLevel: 'aal1' }, error: null }` and `FETCH_FAILED = { data: null, error }` (MfaPage.test.tsx:40-42), so no fixture ever produces `{ data: { currentLevel: null }, error: null }` and nothing would catch it. BUG-269's ledger entry records the factor-list half as fixed and lists no residual for the level.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the guard check the field the comment is about: `if (error || !data || data.currentLevel === null) return null;` at supabase-auth.ts:310, then keep the existing mapping. Add the fixture above to one of the two test files so the branch is pinned by a value auth-js really produces (L-046). If the owner would rather treat a missing `aal` claim as aal1 deliberately, then the prose at supabase-auth.ts:307 and lib/auth.ts:56-59 is what is wrong and must say so (L-053).
findings.requirement: WEBR5-E-1 / WEB-R2-08

findings.title: signOut reports serverNotTold without establishing that this origin's session was removed, and a sibling surface treats that report as the guarantee behind "This computer is signed out"
findings.mechanism: supabase-auth.ts:372-374 returns `{ serverNotTold: true }` immediately after calling `forgetStoredSession(storageKey)`, and never checks that the removal happened. `forgetStoredSession` (supabase-auth.ts:150-157) is best-effort by construction: it returns silently when `storageKey` is null, and it wraps the removal in a try/catch that swallows any throw — including the SecurityError a browser raises on merely touching `globalThis.localStorage` when site data is blocked. In exactly that browser, auth-js's `supportsLocalStorage()` is false, so the client holds the session in `memoryLocalStorageAdapter` (GoTrueClient.js:254-260) and removing a localStorage key cannot reach it: the session survives, and the adapter still reports `serverNotTold: true`. SignOutControl survives this because it re-reads the session itself (SignOutControl.tsx:54-61, 80-85) and takes the STILL_OPEN branch. Its sibling does not: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:790-800 deliberately skips that read on the reported-refusal path and calls it "the adapter's own guarantee" that "this computer is signed out" — re-reading only on the throw branch (`unverified`) — and then shows the parent exactly that sentence on the public page (AccountDeletionPage.tsx:48-49, 69). So the adapter promises a fact it does not establish, and one of its two callers spends the promise as user-facing copy.
findings.repro: Unit test on the real adapter with localStorage made hostile: `Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'localStorage', { get() { throw new DOMException('blocked', 'SecurityError'); }, configurable: true })`, then build the adapter over the App.signout.test.tsx `adapterWith({ error: { message: 'Failed to fetch' } })` fake whose `getSession` still resolves a session. `await adapter.signOut('local')` resolves `{ serverNotTold: true }` while `await adapter.currentSession()` still resolves a session — the report asserts a removal that did not happen. Page-level half, in apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx: with the same hostile storage, run the account-close flow and assert the parent is kept on the portal page (as SignOutControl would) rather than sent to /account-deletion to read "This computer is signed out".
findings.user_impact: In a browser with site data blocked, a parent who closes their account on a shared computer is told the computer is signed out when the session is still live in this tab. On the `pending` closure path the sign-in is not closed server-side either, so the next person at that keyboard can type /app and read the family's children, scans, verdicts and guardian emails — the harm WEB-R4-AUTH-2 exists to prevent. Narrow (it needs blocked storage plus a refused sign-out) but the parent walks away believing the opposite of what is true.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I traced both branches rather than assuming. The adapter's own comment at supabase-auth.ts:144-149 claims only that the removal is attempted on the path where supabase-js leaves the token behind — it never claims success — so the guarantee PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:792-795 relies on is not one the adapter makes; that is a code/prose disagreement (L-053), not a misreading on my part. I confirmed the two callers differ: SignOutControl.tsx:80 computes `open` from `auth.currentSession()` on every path, while PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:807-812 gates the same read behind `unverified`, which is set only in the catch. I also confirmed `forgetStoredSession` cannot report failure: it returns `void` and has no result to inspect (supabase-auth.ts:150-157). App.signout.test.tsx:332-346 pins only the happy case, with a working localStorage, so no existing test covers it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the report say what it can prove. Either (a) have `forgetStoredSession` return a boolean and, when it did not remove the session, re-read `currentSession()` before choosing between `{ serverNotTold: true }` and a stronger 'still open' report so callers can tell the two apart; or (b) leave the adapter as is, delete the "guarantee" claim from PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:790-800, and give that flow the same unconditional `stillSignedIn()` read SignOutControl already does (L-037: the same pre-check on every surface). Whichever is chosen, pin it with the hostile-storage test above.

"a second press only looks like it worked" (SignOutControl.tsx:11-13) is true: GoTrueClient.js:3432-3433 skips the server call entirely when there is no access token and returns { error: null } at :3451, so the old STILL_OPEN advice really was unactionable on that path.

"This computer is signed out" is only said when it has been established: SignOutControl.tsx:80-85 checks open before SignOutControl.tsx:86, and stillSignedIn() fails closed on a throw (SignOutControl.tsx:57-60). With persistSession:true auth-js reads the session from storage on every getSession() (no in-memory cache — GoTrueClient.js:249-265), so removing the key really does make currentSession() null.

The stale-shell worry is closed by the route table, not by luck: App.tsx:160 and :168 mount SignOutControl only under /app or /admin, so navigating to /sign-in unmounts it and the "Signed in as …" line with it — nothing stale is left rendered. Only one alert can be on /sign-in at a time, so the new findByRole('alert') is not ambiguous: AuthLinkNotice returns null when the address carries no auth-link problem (AuthLinkNotice.tsx:63-64), and the sign-out navigation carries no query or hash.

Nothing new is built and unconnected. TWO_STEP_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE is consumed at supabase-auth.ts:333; isTwoStepLookupUnavailable at MfaPage.tsx:41 and PinResetPage.tsx:76; state.signedOutNotice set at SignOutControl.tsx:92 is read at SignInPage.tsx:35 and rendered at :45-49; `lapsed` set at UpdatePasswordPage.tsx:134 feeds mustProve at :107 and draws the Current password field at :171-186.

L-037 for the two-step lookup: grep for verifiedTotpFactorId/assuranceLevel across apps/web/src, apps/mobile/src and packages finds exactly two production surfaces (MfaPage.tsx:32, PinResetPage.tsx:68-69) and both refuse on an unreadable lookup; enrollTotp has one caller (MfaPage.tsx:83). step === 'two_step' cannot fall through to the PIN step with a lost factor id: setStep('two_step') at PinResetPage.tsx:119 only runs on twoStep.state === 'required', and setLookup(twoStep) at :111 sets twoStepFactorId in the same handler, so the guard at :145 cannot be false when step is 'two_step'.

What I could not check, and things I judged below the filing bar:

1. NOT FILED, cross-area observation for the lead. PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:790-800 states that re-reading currentSession() on the reported-refusal path "would only ask supabase-js about its in-memory copy". That is false for this client: with persistSession:true auth-js reads the session from storage on every getSession() (GoTrueClient.js:249-265, and __loadSession uses this.storage), which is exactly why SignOutControl's own read works. The behavioural consequence is HUNT6-F-3; the false sentence is in a file outside my brief, so I have not filed it separately.

2. NOT FILED, low. MfaPage's new 'unavailable' branch (MfaPage.tsx:59-63) renders an ErrorState with no <h1>, so /admin/mfa becomes a headless document in that state — the thing session.tsx:104-105 records as a WEB-R2-06 / WCAG 2.4.6 defect for portal pages. Worth a sweep across all four states rather than a finding against this diff.

3. NOT FILED, low. The signedOutNotice lives in history state, so it is restored on a reload of /sign-in and on a Back navigation to that entry: the parent can be shown "This computer is signed out. We could not tell PencilLift's servers…" again long after it stopped being news. Clearing it (navigate with state: null after the first render) would fix it. Stale rather than untrue, so I did not file it.

4. Claim I checked and did NOT find wanting, though it is loosely worded: SignInPage.tsx:15-16 says "Router state cannot be set by a link — only by a navigation this app made". React Router's <Link state={...}> is a link that sets router state, so the sentence is wrong as stated; but no such link to /sign-in exists, the value is never derived from the URL, and it is rendered as text (SignInPage.tsx:47), so there is no injection to have. Not filed as a defect.

5. Not checkable from here: whether the owner's GoTrue project revokes other sessions on a password change. That decides whether the second clause of the SERVER_NOT_TOLD copy ("change your password if you are worried") is sound. HUNT6-F-1 rests only on the first clause, which is wrong regardless; but the lead should confirm the password-change behaviour before rewriting the copy around it, because if that is off too the notice has no working remedy to offer at all and the honest fix is to build "Sign out everywhere".

6. I ran the web suite once (780/780 pass) — the package's vitest config ignores positional file filters, so the whole suite ran; it wrote test-results/web.json, which .gitignore:20 already excludes. I made no edits; `git status --porcelain` is empty."

findings.title: Account close: a REPORTED sign-out refusal navigates to a page that says "This computer is signed out" without ever checking, and the session is still live in this tab
findings.requirement: WEB-R4-AUTH-2 / ACC-WEB-AUTH-A / WEB-R2-01 (a parent told this computer is signed out really is); L-037 (the same pre-check on EVERY surface); pattern 1 (check the premise the guard rests on)
findings.mechanism: PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:814 gates the session re-read on `unverified`, which is set only inside the catch at :812. On the path the real adapter actually takes — `auth.signOut()` RESOLVING with `{serverNotTold:true}` (supabase-auth.ts:371-374) — `unverified` is false, `stillSignedIn()` (:744) is never called, and :821 pushes to /account-deletion with `signOutRefused: true`, which AccountDeletionPage.tsx:56/69 renders as SERVER_NOT_TOLD (:48) "This computer is signed out. …". The comment at :787-805 justifies skipping the read: "the adapter removes this origin's stored session before it returns `{serverNotTold:true}` … so 'this computer is signed out' is the adapter's own guarantee … re-reading `currentSession()` there would only ask supabase-js about its in-memory copy". That premise is not the fact the sentence needs. `forgetStoredSession` (supabase-auth.ts:143-157) removes ONLY the localStorage key; supabase-js returned its error before `removeCurrentSession()` (the reason forgetStoredSession exists — see its own docstring), so its in-memory session survives and `currentSession()` → `auth.getSession()` (supabase-auth.ts:341-346) still answers a live ParentSession. The codebase says so itself: App.signout.test.tsx's `adapterWith` (the real adapter over a labeled fake client) gives a `getSession` that ALWAYS returns a session, and drives this exact closure flow through it at App.signout.test.tsx:400-427 — so in the repo's own model of production the page asserts "signed out" over a readable session. SignOutControl.tsx:80-94 treats the identical adapter outcome the opposite way: it calls `stillSignedIn()` on EVERY path and, when the session is still readable, stays put and says "you are still signed in on this computer" (App.signout.test.tsx:187-204 pins that for `refuse: 'reported'`, whose fake deliberately leaves the session in place). Two callers of one adapter outcome, opposite claims; the close flow's is the false one. Aggravating: :821 is a PUSH (SignOutControl uses `replace: true`), so one Back returns to /app/privacy, where RequireParent (session.tsx:117-130) re-reads `currentSession()`, gets the in-memory session and renders the portal again with "Signed in as p•••@…".
findings.repro: In PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx, reuse `renderWithRealDeletionPage` with an auth that models the real adapter after a refused sign-out: `currentSession: () => Promise.resolve({accessToken:'t', email:'parent@example.test'})` (never cleared) and `signOut: () => Promise.resolve({serverNotTold: true as const})`; api.send('/v1/account/close') → `{status:'pending', signOut:true}` (the owner path, where the sign-in is deliberately still usable until the purge). Tick the box, press "Delete my account". Today: the public page renders "This computer is signed out." while `await auth.currentSession()` is still non-null — the existing test at PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1240-1285 asserts exactly that sentence, so it pins the defect. Required: the flow stays on /app/privacy and says "you are still signed in on this computer" (as it already does for the thrown case at :814), and `screen.queryByText(/this computer is signed out/i)` is null. Second assertion for the push: after the navigation, `router.navigate(-1)` lands back on /app/privacy with the portal rendered.
findings.user_impact: A parent on a shared family, school or library computer closes their account, reads "This computer is signed out", and walks away — while this browser tab still holds a usable parent session. The next person presses Back and is inside the parent portal again, seeing the signed-in account line, the deletion request's status, the family's export list and the family's safety reports including the free-text notes; on the owner/`pending` path the session stays valid for further API calls until the purge finishes, because that sign-in is closed only afterwards. The product states the one fact it has not checked, in the exact situation the check exists for.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: (a) `stillSignedIn()` exists at :744 but is unreachable unless the catch at :810-813 ran; (b) AccountDeletionPage.tsx:56 gates the sentence only on `closed !== null`, never on a session check; (c) the three new tests that cover this path (PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:1022-1046, :1240-1285) all supply an auth whose `currentSession` keeps returning a session and assert the page DOES say "this computer is signed out", so the suite locks the wrong behaviour in rather than catching it; (d) App.signout.test.tsx:400-427 runs the real adapter through this flow over a client whose `getSession` always answers and asserts only 'deletion page: closed'; (e) session.tsx's `signOutOnUnauthenticated` only reacts to a 401 and on the `pending` path there is none, because that session is deliberately still valid.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `unverified &&` guard at :814 so the session is re-read on BOTH refusal paths, exactly as SignOutControl.tsx:80 does — a session still readable keeps the parent on the privacy page with `stillSignedInCopy(status)` (where the portal's own Sign out is), a session really gone travels to the public page with `signOutRefused`. Delete the paragraph at :795-805 that argues the in-memory copy can be ignored; it is the fact the sentence is about. Also make :821 `{ replace: true }` so a closed account cannot be re-entered with Back. If the lead prefers to make the adapter's guarantee real instead, `signOut` must also drop supabase-js's in-memory session (not just the storage key) before returning `{serverNotTold:true}`, and App.signout.test.tsx's `adapterWith` fake must stop answering `getSession` after a refusal — but the page must still not assert what it has not read.

findings.requirement: HUNT5-F-2 / L-037 (the same pre-check on EVERY surface); spec P4 / AC_UX_02 honest copy about what is kept and what is deleted

The other consumer, ChildrenPage.tsx:308, is unguarded: it renders `Status: {childStatusLabel(child.status)}` unconditionally, two lines above the deletion notice at :309-320 that says the child's data is being deleted. `childStatusLabel` has exactly these two callers (grep: ChildrenPage.tsx:308, FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:149), so the sibling was in the same diff and in the same file that defines the label.

For the full L-037 sweep the same label is printed for a deletion-pending child by RewardsPage.tsx:400-404 ('(archived — history only)') and by the mobile view model at apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:19-27, neither of which branches on the flag.

findings.title: HUNT5-F-1's family test synchronises on an assertion that cannot fail: the form's own help text contains "Europe/Berlin"
findings.requirement: L-054 (an assertion is only as good as the string and source it searches); test integrity — the step that proves the race must be checked, not assumed
findings.mechanism: The new test's only check that guardian B's zone has landed under the open form is `await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getAllByText(/Europe\/Berlin/).length).toBeGreaterThan(0))` at :174. The form is open at that point (`openForm` was called at :171), and EditFamilyForm's hint renders `America/Chicago or Europe/Berlin` (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:255-259). testing-library's default matcher matches that `` element's own text, so the assertion is already satisfied before the retry's GET resolves and can never go red. The assertion after it (:175, the field still reads America/Chicago) holds whether or not the reload landed, because the field is seeded. So nothing in the test establishes the precondition the whole case is about; that the case still bites on the pre-fix code depends only on incidental microtask flushing inside the following `user.clear`/`user.type` calls. With a deferred responder — the very technique this round's own download test adopted (PrivacyControlsPage.download.test.tsx:76-83) — the reload would land after the save and the test would pass green with `changes()` diffing against the live prop again.
findings.repro: Run the case with the responder for the third GET deferred until after the second PATCH (resolve it from a stored `resolve` instead of `Promise.resolve`) and revert FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:196-199 to diff against `data` rather than `seed`: the vacuous waitFor still passes, and `expect(sends[1]!.body).toEqual({displayName:'The Riveras'})` passes too, because `data` was never replaced. The defect HUNT5-F-1 was filed for is then green.
findings.user_impact: None directly; the guard against re-introducing a silent revert of the family time zone — the value every practice release, weekly review and school report is planned in — rests on test timing rather than on a checked fact, so the next refactor of the fake API can quietly un-cover it.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: (a) there is no other assertion in the case that distinguishes the reloaded family from the original — :175 and :177 both read the seeded field, and the final body assertion at :183 is satisfied by BOTH the fixed and the unfixed code when the reload has not landed; (b) `family.displayName` is 'Test Family' in both fixtures (:27, :151) so the heading/summary give no second signal either; (c) FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx has no `afterEach` that would clear the DOM between the openForm and the waitFor.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert on the summary node the reload actually changes, e.g. `await screen.findByText('Time zone: Europe/Berlin')` (the paragraph at FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:100 renders exactly that text), or require two matches (`getAllByText(/Europe\/Berlin/).length` ≥ 2) so the static hint alone is not enough. Then re-run with FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:196-199 reverted to `data` and confirm the case goes red.

findings.title: HUNT5-F-1's child test synchronises on an assertion that cannot fail: the open grade select always contains "Grade 4"
findings.requirement: L-054; test integrity — same defect as HUNT6-G-3, in the sibling test of the same fix

findings.repro: Defer the second GET in `fakeApi` (ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:61-64) until after the PATCH, and revert the diff basis at ChildrenPage.tsx:529-531 from `seed` back to `child`: line 319 still passes, and `expect(sends.find(c => c.method === 'PATCH')!.body).toEqual({nickname:'Riley R.'})` also passes, because `child` was never refreshed. findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: (a) the earlier assertions at :312-313 read the seeded field values, which are identical before and after the reload; (b) the `later` overview at :304-307 keeps the nickname 'Riley', so `card('Riley')` and the `save Riley` button name give no second signal; (c) the final body assertion at :331 is satisfied by the unfixed code whenever the reload has not landed, so nothing else in the case can go red.

findings.title: HUNT5-F-3 guarded the edit form on status but not the archive confirmation in the same card, so "Yes, archive" survives a reload that made the child deletion-pending
findings.requirement: L-037 / L-042 (no surface offers an action the server refuses); HUNT5-F-3's own stated goal
findings.mechanism: HUNT5-F-3 added `child.status !== 'archived' && !deletionPending` to the edit form's render condition (ChildrenPage.tsx:419) with the comment at :415-418: "a change from ANY source … closes a form the server would refuse to save". The archive confirmation at :422-452 — the other open panel in the same card, hidden by the same button row at :379-381 — got no such condition. So when a reload lands `deletionPending: true` (the other guardian filed a child deletion) while the confirmation is open, the card renders the notice at :309 ("nothing can be changed, paired or activated for them"), hides Edit/Archive, hides the edit form, and still shows a live "Yes, archive Riley" plus the promise "You can activate them again later while a paid slot is free" (:428-432). Pressing it POSTs /v1/children/:id/archive, where `visibleChild` excludes a child under an open deletion (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:111-116, 515-516) and the route answers NOT_FOUND 'Child not found'.

Click 'Archive Riley' to open the confirmation, then add a draft child in the Add-a-child form (which triggers the reload), then assert `within(riley).queryByRole('button', {name:/yes, archive Riley/i})` is null. It is present today, and clicking it puts 'Child not found' in the card's ActionFeedback.
findings.user_impact: A parent is shown, under a notice saying nothing can be changed for this child, a confirmation button that promises the child can be reactivated later — and pressing it answers "Child not found" for a child whose card is on screen. The same gap leaves a live archive confirmation on an already-archived child (harmless: the route is idempotent), so only the deletion-pending case misleads.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: (a) the button row is hidden at :379-381 for archived/deletionPending, but the confirmation block at :422 is a separate sibling with no status condition; (b) `confirmArchive` is cleared only by a successful archive (:262) or the 'Keep … as they are' button (:448-451), never by a status change; (c) the buttons are disabled only while `busy !== null` (:437, :446) and `busy` is null while the confirmation merely sits open, so the parent can trigger the reload from the Add-a-child form in between; (d) no test in ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx or ChildrenPage.profile.test.tsx opens the confirmation and then reloads.
findings.suggested_fix: Give :422 the same condition as :419 (`confirmArchive && child.status !== 'archived' && !deletionPending`), and clear `confirmArchive` wherever `setEditing(false)` is cleared, so one rule covers every open panel in the card. The pairing-code panel at :467-474 has the same shape and should be reviewed with it.

findings.title: The refusal notice on the public deletion page gives advice that cannot be followed when the account has just been closed
findings.requirement: AC_UX_02 / spec P14 honest copy that points somewhere useful; L-053 (decide which of code and prose is TRUE)
findings.mechanism: SERVER_NOT_TOLD (:48) is reused word for word from SignOutControl.tsx:15-16, where it is written for an ordinary sign-out and the parent's ACCOUNT still exists: "…so sign out on your phone, or change your password if you are worried." AccountDeletionPage renders it for both closure outcomes (:66-69 branches the closure line on `closed`/`pending` but not the refusal line), and the doc comment at :41-47 justifies the reuse with "the two paths report the same fact". They do not. `status: 'closed'` is returned only after `closeNow` succeeded, i.e. `authAdmin.closeUser(userId)` closed the sign-in (apps/api/src/routes/account.ts:106-110, 180-196). There is then no account to sign into on the phone and no password to change — the parent is told, on the screen confirming their account is deleted, to do two things the product has just made impossible.
findings.repro: PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx, copy the case at :1240-1285 (`renderWithRealDeletionPage`, `signOut: () => Promise.resolve({serverNotTold:true})`) but answer `/v1/account/close` with `{status:'closed', signOut:true}`. Assert `expect(notice.textContent).not.toMatch(/change your password/i)` while the closure line still reads ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed. It fails today: the notice says the account is closed and then tells the parent to change its password.
findings.user_impact: A parent who has just deleted their sign-in is told to change its password or sign out on their phone. Either they try and cannot (the sign-in no longer works), and conclude the closure went wrong, or they contact support about a session the product cannot help them with.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: (a) :56 gates the sentence only on `closed !== null`, not on which of the two closure outcomes it is; (b) :66-69 branch the closure line on the outcome but hand the refusal line the same string either way; (c) the new test at :1240-1285 uses `status: 'pending'` only — the one outcome on which the advice is meaningful — so the 'closed' combination is untested; (d) the comment at :43-46 asserts "a session elsewhere may still work" unconditionally, which is the clause that makes the advice sound useful, and it is qualified only for `pending`.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the refusal line by outcome: on `pending` keep SignOutControl's sentence (the sign-in is genuinely still open until the purge finishes); on `closed` say only that the servers were not told to end this session and that the sign-in is closed, so nothing further is needed — and correct the comment at :43-46, which currently asserts a property only the `pending` path has. Put the two strings in packages/contracts/src/account.ts beside ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY so the portal and the app cannot drift.

findings.title: A HUNT5-N6 test comment says the closure is reported by the action outcome, which the code it tests deletes two lines earlier
findings.requirement: L-053 / pattern 4 (prose asserting a property the code does not have)
findings.mechanism: The comment at :1080-1081 reads "the closure itself is still reported here (the action outcome carries it)" and introduces the assertion at :1085 (`/your PencilLift account is closed/i`). The outcome does not carry it: PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:817 calls `action.setOutcome(null)` before setting `sessionStillOpen`, and the same test asserts that at :1092-1093 (`not.toContain(ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed)` / `.pending`) with its own comment explaining why the outcome must be gone. The sentence :1085 matches is `stillSignedInCopy`'s restatement (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:723-730), which exists precisely because the outcome is dropped.
findings.repro: Not a runtime defect: `grep -n "the action outcome carries it" apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx` → :1081, then read PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:817 and the same file's :1092-1093. The two statements in one test contradict each other.
findings.user_impact: None for a parent. A maintainer reading this test believes the closure sentence comes from the action outcome and may delete `stillSignedInCopy`'s closure clause (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:723-728) as duplication, which silently leaves the parent on this path with no statement that their account was closed at all — and :1085 would then fail for a reason the comment cannot explain.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: the comment is the only explanation of where :1085's text comes from, and the corrective comment at :1088-1093 is about a different assertion (that the outcome is absent), so a reader gets both claims and no reconciliation; nothing in the file points at `stillSignedInCopy` as the source.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comment to say the closure clause is restated by `stillSignedInCopy` because the success outcome is dropped (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:817), and cite the constant so the next reader follows it to the right place.

findings.title: After a concurrent change lands under an open edit form, Save is disabled for the value the form is showing, with nothing on screen to explain it
findings.requirement: WEBR4-03 / HUNT5-F-1 — the cost the seed fix introduced and nothing tells the parent about; AC_UX_02 (no dead control without an honest explanation)
findings.mechanism: `nothingChanged` now diffs the fields against `seed` (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:196-200; ChildrenPage.tsx:529-532) and the submit button is `disabled={busy || nothingChanged}` (:261 / ChildrenPage.tsx:586). When the other guardian's value lands under the open form, the field keeps showing the seeded value and the summary above shows the new one (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:100), so a parent who wants the value the form is displaying finds Save greyed out and nothing saying why. Concretely (the exact state the new test at FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx:146-183 sets up): seed zone America/Chicago, guardian B sets Europe/Berlin, the summary reads Europe/Berlin, the field reads America/Chicago, and pressing Save is impossible — the only route through is Cancel, reopen (which reseeds to Europe/Berlin) and retype. Before this round the button was ENABLED in that state; it reverted the zone, which is why HUNT5-F-1 was filed, so the round traded a silent revert for a silently inert control. The same holds for the child's grade at ChildrenPage.tsx:532/586.
findings.repro: Extend the new case at FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx:147: after the retry lands `moved` (Europe/Berlin), without touching the name, assert `expect(screen.getByRole('button', {name:/^save family details$/i})).toHaveProperty('disabled', false)` — it is `true`, so a parent cannot save the America/Chicago the field is showing them, and no `role="alert"` or note appears anywhere in the form.
findings.user_impact: A parent trying to put the family time zone back — the zone every practice release, weekly review and school report is planned in — or to correct a child's grade after the other guardian changed it, sees the value they want already in the field, a greyed-out Save, and no explanation. Most will conclude the page is broken rather than discover that closing and reopening the form is what unblocks it.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and it does NOT prevent this: (a) nothing compares `seed` with the live prop, so no notice is rendered when they diverge (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:224-265, ChildrenPage.tsx:547-590 have no such branch); (b) the existing 'keeps the save button disabled while nothing has been changed' cases (FamilyDashboardPage.save.test.tsx:135-143, ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:243-261) only cover the no-concurrency case, where disabled is right; (c) the new HUNT5-F-1 cases assert the field value (:175, :177) and the request body (:183), never the button's enabled state after the divergence; (d) the form is not remounted by the reload — the card is keyed on `child.id` (ChildrenPage.tsx:153) and EditFamilyForm is mounted from `editing` alone (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:114) — so the seed cannot refresh itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Track touched-ness explicitly instead of inferring it from a diff: keep a per-field `touched` flag, send only touched fields (which keeps WEBR4-03/HUNT5-F-1 intact) and base the disabled state on "nothing touched" rather than on "equal to the seed". Then, when `seed` and the live prop disagree on a field, say so in the form ("Another guardian changed the time zone to Europe/Berlin while this form was open") with a control to reseed, so the stale value is never silently authoritative.

sweeps_sound: HUNT5-F-7's download window is sound and free of cross-clock arithmetic: PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:653-654 computes `Date.now() - link.requestedAt` with both ends on the device clock, and `requestedAt` (:661) is captured before `api.get`, so the drop instant (send + 60s) is never later than the signature's death (sign + 60s) because the API signs at or after the request was sent (apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts:49-51). L-038 holds; I tried and could not build a skew that leaves a dead URL clickable.
LINK_WINDOW_MS = 60_000 (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:600) really does mirror DOWNLOAD_URL_SECONDS = 60 (apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts:8) — the comment's claim checks out.
