findings.title: The HUNT5-H-1 fix rests on "the screens key their load on the client" — the Practice planner does not, so the next adult keeps the previous family's children with no refetch at all
findings.requirement: spec P3 / AC_ACCESS_07 (a parent screen never shows another adult's family data); MOB-R4-LOCK-04; BUG-289
findings.mechanism: The whole fix is a premise about the screens: apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:292-298 says a moved identity "publishes fresh state, which is what makes the screen refetch" because "the screens key their load on the client", and apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:73-78 repeats it. One parent screen does not. app/(parent)/planner.tsx:63-78 has its own loader whose effect deps are `[key, version]` — `key` is the literal 'family' (planner.tsx:83) or a path built from the child id (planner.tsx:133-140), and `version` is a manual counter bumped only by `reload()`. Neither depends on the client. PlannerScreen renders `<Planner api={access.api} />` (planner.tsx:57), so when the gate publishes a new `{status:'ready', api}` (ui.tsx:299-312) Planner re-renders with parent B's client, the effect never re-runs, and NO request is made; `ChildPlan` is keyed by `child.id` (planner.tsx:117), so it is not remounted either. Result: publishing fresh state changes nothing on this screen. Parent A's FamilyOverview — every child's nickname, grade and age band, the family time zone — plus A's selected child's subject toggles and learning schedule stay rendered for parent B indefinitely, with no expiry and no PIN in between. The fix was verified on the one screen its own test comment names (screens-r2.review.test.ts:196-201 cites app/(parent)/home.tsx) and assumed for the rest (L-037).
findings.repro: Unit level: render `Planner` (app/(parent)/planner.tsx:82) with `api1`, let `GET /v1/family` resolve with family A (children: 'Riley', 'Sam'); then re-render the same mounted component with `api2` (a client whose token source is parent B). Assert a second `GET /v1/family` was issued and that 'Riley' is no longer rendered — today no second request is sent and A's nicknames stay. End to end: A signs in on a paired tablet, home → 'Learning planner' (push), A's 5-minute unlock lapses, A saves the schedule → STEP_UP_REQUIRED → the ErrorBox at planner.tsx:467 offers 'Unlock with parent PIN' → ui.tsx:240 `router.push('/(parent)/unlock')` (a PUSH, so the planner stays mounted); A's session is ended from the portal ("sign out everywhere") → unlock.tsx:67-70 shows the sign-in prompt → B signs in (replace), B's PIN → unlock.tsx:101 `router.replace('/(parent)/home')`; B taps the header back arrow onto the planner: focus re-check publishes fresh state, and B reads A's children and A's child's practice plan.
findings.user_impact: On any device two parents have used (a handed-on family tablet, a school loaner, a resold phone), the second parent reads the first family's children — names, grades, age bands — and that family's practice schedule on the Learning planner screen, for as long as the screen stays in the stack. This is precisely the harm BUG-289 was filed for and recorded as closed.
findings.not_a_false_positive: (a) The gate really does publish a new state object for a moved identity — ui.tsx:299-312 — so the defect is downstream of the fix, not in it. (b) Planner is not remounted: `access.status` stays 'ready' across the swap (planner.tsx:47-57) and React reconciles the same element type at the same position, so useApiLoad's state survives. (c) Nothing else invalidates it: useApiLoad's deps are `[key, version]` (planner.tsx:78), `version` moves only through `reload()`, which is wired to the error-path retry buttons and post-edit callbacks (planner.tsx:99/150/165) — not to the client. (d) No test would catch it: apps/mobile/src/family/screens.test.ts:33-49 asserts only planner copy, and the new source assertions in screens-r2.review.test.ts:203-220 read ui.tsx only. (e) `clearAdultCaches()` cannot save it: apps/mobile/src/family/parent-session.ts:16/50 runs only registered clearers, and the planner registers none (BUG-288 records this). (f) The mounted-underneath state is reachable — ui.tsx:240 is a push, not a replace, and unlock.tsx:101 replaces only the top route, so deeper parent screens stay mounted.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the planner's loads on the client the gate published: make useApiLoad's effect deps `[api, key, version]` (pass the client in, or fold the hook into ui.tsx's `useLoad`, which is already keyed on a `useCallback(..., [api])`). Then add the assertion that was missing: every parent screen's loader must invalidate on the client — a source-level check over app/(parent)/*.tsx in screens-r2.review.test.ts, so the next screen added cannot opt out silently.

findings.title: The refetch the fix triggers keeps the previous adult's rows on screen while it runs, so "never keeps its rows" is untrue of every useLoad screen
findings.requirement: spec P3 / AC_ACCESS_07; the claims at mode.ts:98, app-session.ts:85 and ui.tsx:347-348
findings.mechanism: `useLoad`'s run deliberately preserves a ready state: apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:514 `setState((s) => (s.status === 'ready' ? s : { status: 'loading' }))`. When the gate publishes fresh state for a moved identity (ui.tsx:299-312), the screen's content component is NOT remounted — children.tsx:54 renders `{access.status === 'ready' ? <ChildrenContent api={access.api} /> : null}`, the same element type at the same position — so only the `api` prop changes, `load` (children.tsx:62, `useCallback(..., [api])`) changes, `run` re-runs, and line 514 keeps parent A's `FamilyOverview` rendered until the new request settles: up to DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 20 s (packages/contracts/src/client.ts:48), and longer on a retry loop. So the prose in this diff is wrong in three places: mode.ts:98 and app-session.ts:85 say an identity move "costs a mounted screen one refetch and never keeps its rows", and ui.tsx:347-348 says "what it can no longer do is serve that state to a different adult" — it does serve it, for the duration of the refetch. Component state that is not keyed survives even the refetch: `AddChild` (children.tsx:406) is at a fixed position, so a nickname A typed and never submitted stays in the input for B. app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:90-104 and app/(parent)/rewards.tsx:64-76 have the same shape (no 'loading' reset before the fetch), so the window is not specific to useLoad.
findings.repro: Mount `ChildrenContent` (app/(parent)/children.tsx:60) with `api1`; resolve `GET /v1/family` as family A ('Riley'). Change the prop to `api2` whose `GET /v1/family` does not resolve. Assert that 'Riley' is no longer rendered — today it is, until the 20 s timeout fires. Source-level equivalent while the hook cannot be rendered: assert `useLoad` drops `data` when the `load` identity changes (a load-owner ref beside the state), which is the same shape as the `publishedUnder` capture the gate now uses.
findings.user_impact: On a handed-on tablet the second parent still reads the first family's children (nicknames, grades, age bands) for the length of one request — routinely a second or two, up to 20 s on a poor connection — and keeps an unsubmitted nickname the previous adult typed. BUG-289's residual column records only that the hook cannot be rendered in the suite; it does not record that the published-fresh state leaves the rows on screen, so the record understates what shipped.
findings.not_a_false_positive: (a) I checked for a remount: neither children.tsx:54 nor home/plan/devices/school/support change element type or add a key on the identity, so React preserves useLoad's state. (b) I checked for a clearer: apps/mobile/src/family/parent-session.ts:50 runs only registered clearers and only revenuecat.ts and app/(parent)/resources.tsx:195 register one — and that path fires on sign-out, not on the identity move that a re-check acts on. (c) I checked that this is not already handled by a 'loading' reset: app/(parent)/resources.tsx:211 does `setState({status:'loading'})` before its fetch, which is exactly what ui.tsx:514 does not do, so the codebase has both shapes and the safe one is not in the shared hook. (d) No existing test asserts either way; the only nearby assertions (screens-r2.review.test.ts:203-220) pin the gate's reuse condition, not what the screen renders during the refetch.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the state's owner explicit inside useLoad, the same lesson as L-051: keep a ref of the `load` the current data was produced by, and when `load` changes, drop to `{status:'loading'}` instead of preserving 'ready' (a manual `reload()` keeps today's no-flash behaviour, because the identity of `load` has not changed). Alternatively, have the gate hand screens the identity and key the ready subtree on it, which also clears unkeyed drafts. Then correct the three prose claims (mode.ts:98, app-session.ts:85, ui.tsx:347-348) to say what the code does.

findings.title: The rewritten deletion notice tells the family's other adult that THEY asked for the child's data to be deleted, which deletionPending cannot establish
findings.requirement: spec P4 / honesty of user-facing copy (the requirement HUNT5-H-2 and HUNT5-H-3 were filed under)
findings.mechanism: The notice now asserts the reader's own act: app/(parent)/children.tsx:243 "You asked for {row.nickname}’s data to be deleted." The flag it is rendered from carries no such fact — apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:243 sends `deletionPending: ch.deletion_pending`, computed at family.ts:137-146 as `exists (… deletion_requests d where d.family_id = c.family_id and (d.scope = 'family' or d.target_child_id = c.id) and d.status in ('requested','processing'))`, with no reference to the caller. And the request need not be the reader's: apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:583-586 states the rule — "Only the owner may request [a family deletion]. Any guardian may delete a child's data" — and supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:97-99 enforces the same, while a child-scope request touches only child_profiles (0840:128) and leaves every membership active (only the family scope revokes them, 0840:124-126). So after guardian A deletes one child's data, guardian B opens Children, is served the same `deletionPending: true`, and is told they asked for it. The premise-checking the round did for HUNT5-H-3 (which scope can reach this screen) was not repeated for the new claim (which PERSON the flag names), and the new tests now pin the untrue wording: screens-r2.review.test.ts:282 `expect(notice).toMatch(/You\s+asked\s+for\s+\{row\.nickname\}/)`.
findings.repro: API/contract test: family with owner A and guardian B (guardians.ts invite/accept path), children Riley and Sam. As A, `POST /v1/privacy/deletion {scope:'child', childId: riley}`. As B, `GET /v1/family` → Riley comes back with `deletionPending: true` and nothing that says who asked. Render the Children screen for B: the card reads "You asked for Riley’s data to be deleted." A screen-level assertion that the notice does not claim the reader made the request (or that it uses the requester the server names) is red today on both clients.
findings.user_impact: The adult who did not request the deletion is told, in the app, that they did — on the most alarming notice this screen carries. A co-parent reads it as their own action (or as their account having been used by someone else), and the sentence that follows sends them to support to undo something they never asked for, while the parent who did ask may never see the notice on their own device.
findings.not_a_false_positive: (a) I checked whether the response could carry the requester: `deletion_requests.requested_by` IS recorded (0840:106-107), but GET /v1/family never exposes it (family.ts:236-245), so the screen cannot know — the copy is an assumption, not a lookup. (b) I checked whether a second adult can reach this screen: only a family-scope request revokes memberships (0840:124-126), and that is the state HUNT5-H-3 correctly proved unreachable here; a child-scope request leaves B's membership active, so GET /v1/family answers B normally. (c) I checked that two-adult families are live, not theoretical: apps/web/src/pages/app/GuardiansPage.invite.test.tsx and apps/api/src/routes/guardians.ts:577 ship the invite/accept flow, and FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:72 links 'Guardians'. (d) The previous wording did not have this defect — it was requester-neutral ("A deletion request covering {row.nickname} is open"), so this is new in this diff. (e) No test guards it; the new ones pin it in place (screens-r2.review.test.ts:282, children-screen.test.ts:93-94 only forbid 'cancel').
findings.suggested_fix: Make the sentence true of any adult who can see it — "A data deletion request covering {nickname} is open" followed by the same, correct "Processing has already stopped … Deletion can’t be undone from the app: if you did not mean it, contact support straight away" — and change the assertion to pin the requester-neutral form. If naming the requester is wanted, add it to the contract instead (e.g. `deletionRequestedByMe`) and branch the copy on it; the server already stores `requested_by`.

findings.title: The background lock switches adult screen privacy OFF from inside the 'background' handler, while an adult screen is still the last rendered frame
findings.requirement: MOB-R2-01 / MOB-R2-05 (screen privacy: app-switcher and screenshot protection for adult screens)
findings.mechanism: BUG-287's fix adds `await effects.setScreenPrivacy(false)` to the paired branch of lockParentAreaOnDevice (apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:147), and that function's other caller is the backgrounding handler: apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts:95-107 runs it on AppState 'background'. runtime.ts:158-171 maps `false` to `allowScreenCaptureAsync()` + `disableAppSwitcherProtectionAsync()`. So on a paired family tablet the app now removes app-switcher protection at the one instant it exists for — the transition the OS snapshots — and the frame on screen is still the adult one: `resetNavigationToChildHome()` (mode.ts:142) is a JS `router.replace` (runtime.ts:140-143) that cannot paint while the app is suspended, so the child home is rendered only on the next foreground. The pre-fix code could not lose this race, because protection stayed on. The fix's own reasoning (mode.ts:143-146) is about the state the CHILD later holds the tablet in, which argues for switching privacy off when the child space comes into view, not while the adult screen is being backgrounded.
findings.repro: iOS/Android device test: sign in, unlock, open a parent screen (e.g. Children with a child listed) on a tablet holding a child pairing, then background the app with the app switcher open. Inspect the app-switcher card: with the ordering above it can show the parent screen rather than the protected placeholder, and a screenshot taken from the switcher succeeds. A unit-level guard is also possible: assert that the background path (app-session.ts:101-107) does not call `setScreenPrivacy(false)` before the app is active again — e.g. that lockParentAreaOnDevice takes the privacy change as a deferred effect applied on the next 'active'.
findings.user_impact: After a grown-up has been in the parent area, backgrounding the tablet can leave the adult screen (children's names and grades, plan and billing, privacy) visible as the app-switcher card and capturable by screenshot — on the device a child is about to hold. The protection the product claims for adult screens is dropped at exactly the moment it is needed.
findings.not_a_false_positive: (a) Nothing defers the call: mode.ts:147 is awaited inside the same handler chain that AppState 'background' starts (app-session.ts:101-107), and nothing re-enables protection before the next 'active'. (b) Nothing else repaints first: the only navigation is the JS `router.replace` at runtime.ts:140-143, which cannot render while the app is backgrounded, so the last rendered frame is the parent screen. (c) `useChildModeOnFocus` cannot help — mode 'child' is already written (mode.ts:141), which is the very reason BUG-287 was filed. (d) The new test only asserts that 'privacy:false' is among the lock's calls (mode-r2.review.test.ts:234) — it says nothing about when, so it passes for both orderings. (e) The unpaired branch is untouched (mode.ts:148-151), so this is specific to the paired-tablet path the fix added.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the fix's outcome but move its moment: record that the child space owes a `setScreenPrivacy(false)` and apply it when the app is next active (or when the child home mounts — a child-side focus effect that does not depend on mode still being 'parent'), so adult protection survives the backgrounding snapshot and the child's own space still allows screenshots, recording and casting. Assert the ordering, not just the call.

sweeps_sound: noteParentIdentity's rule is sound as written: mode.ts:100-104 no-ops only on the same non-null id, and I could not build a transition (A→A, A→null→B, null→null, unreadable→unreadable) where state published for one adult stays current for another, because every local sign-in is preceded by a local sign-out (parent-auth.ts:142 → app-session.ts:63-79) and the gate falls to 'no_session' as soon as the token source is unregistered (ui.tsx:283-286).

The React-updater ordering re-fix holds: ui.tsx:306 captures `readyIdentity.current` into a local BEFORE setAccess and writes the new value only at ui.tsx:312, so the updater cannot compare the new identity with itself, whichever way React schedules it; the source-level assertions at screens-r2.review.test.ts:222-241 bite on that exact ordering (both the positive sequence and the not.toMatch on reading the ref inside the updater).

The sign-out branch closes the window synchronously: app-session.ts:76 `noteParentIdentity(null)` runs before any await, so the async id read on the signed-in branch (app-session.ts:90-91) cannot leave a gap in which a screen published for the previous adult reads as current. I tried out-of-order resolution of two userId() reads and could only produce extra refetches, never a reuse.

The new screen-privacy tests bite: the fixture records `privacy:${on}` (mode-r2.review.test.ts:57-60) and uses a fresh effects object for the lock, so deleting mode.ts:147 turns the paired test red, and moving the call out of the branch turns the unpaired negative test red (mode-r2.review.test.ts:234, 248).

The deletion-notice negative assertions satisfy L-054: both slices are scoped to the notice and guarded against an empty match (children-screen.test.ts:90-92, screens-r2.review.test.ts:269-271), the ranges are unbounded `[\s\S]*?`/`[^]*?` to the first `</Notice>`, the apostrophe in `can’t` matches the rendered character, and re-adding either the cancel promise or the whole-family hedge turns them red.

family-view.test.ts's docFor regex cannot silently pass: `((?:(?!\*/)[\s\S])*)` cannot cross a comment end, so it binds to the doc comment immediately above the declaration, and a renamed or missing declaration yields '' which fails `toMatch(/archived/i)` (family-view.test.ts:190-203).

The family-view doc claims are true of the code they describe: apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:492 really clears `archived_at` for any profile that is not already active (family.ts:473), so 'a draft, or an archived child' at family-view.ts:40-50 matches behaviour, and childRows' widened `canActivate` (family-view.ts:90) has exactly two consumers — children.tsx:274 (guarded by deletionPending) and home.tsx:89, which renders no control.

The STORAGE_KEYS comment rewritten for BUG-248 is true of child-session.ts: the persisted record is `{id, mintedAtMs}` written on every path (child-session.ts:238-240) and an id older than REQUEST_ID_MAX_AGE_MS is replaced rather than presented (child-session.ts:222-229), so mode.ts:39-49 describes the code that exists.

HUNT5-H-3's premise really holds: a family-scope request revokes every active membership in the same transaction as the tombstone (0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:124-126), so currentFamilyId cannot answer for any adult of that family and the hedge it removed named an unreachable state.

L-042 is respected by the deletion-pending row: the child stays listed and the ACTIONS are refused both client-side (children.tsx:260, 274, 285) and server-side (family.ts:354-357), rather than the row being hidden.
L-007 is intact: app-session.ts registers only `childSession.accessToken` for child sources (lines 53-54) and adds no second refresher; the new identity code touches parent state only.
I-mobile-identity.notes:
Scope and method: I read all ten of my files whole plus the code they depend on (the gate's consumers, the nine parent screens' loaders, parent-auth, runtime, child-session, the family and privacy API routes, migration 0840) and the ledger rows for this diff (BUG-287..293) and L-050..L-054 before filing. I did NOT run any test suite — the brief is read-only and a vitest run writes cache files — so every finding is a source trace, not an observed red test; each repro is written so it can become one.

What I could not check: (1) the app-switcher timing in HUNT6-I-4 depends on expo-screen-capture's native overlay lifecycle versus iOS's snapshot instant, and expo-screen-capture is not installed in this checkout, so I could not read its implementation or measure the race — the source-level fact (protection is disabled from inside the 'background' handler while the adult frame is the last painted one) is certain, the resulting card contents are not, which is why I filed it low. (2) useParentAccess and useLoad still cannot be rendered in these suites (the vitest project cannot import react-native), an accepted residual on BUG-289 — so HUNT6-I-1 and HUNT6-I-2 would need either a react-dom-free extraction of the loaders or the screens' own render tests.

Two things I decided NOT to file. First, mode-r2.review.test.ts:459-461 asserts `parentStateStillCurrent(parentIdentityGeneration())` is true — a value the test itself computed, which is close to the unfailable-assertion pattern the brief warns about; it is weak documentation rather than a check, but it can still fail under a mis-implemented comparison, and the neighbouring assertions in that block bite hard, so it is not a defect on its own. Second, the mobile notice drops the web's sentence "You can follow it on the privacy page" and carries a 'Privacy and data' button instead, so children.tsx:237-238's claim that the two inline links "are the only difference" is a slight simplification, not an untrue claim about behaviour. I also checked that "contact support straight away" points somewhere live and useful (app/(parent)/support.tsx:63-120 offers a new case), even though the purge job is enqueued with no delay (0840:132-135) — the copy promises only contact, never an undo, so I did not file it.

Ordering for the lead: HUNT6-I-1 and HUNT6-I-2 are the same property (BUG-289's) still partly broken, and a single fix shape closes both — invalidate a screen's loaded data on the client the gate publishes, in one shared hook, and assert it for every parent screen rather than for the one screen the test comment names.

findings.title: The new `signedOut` flag cannot observe a failed device sign-out, so HUNT5-N6's fix is inert in the case it names
findings.requirement: MOB-R2-06 / L-037 / L-053: a claim about the device in front of the parent must be true, and the portal's distinction must hold on the app too
findings.mechanism: privacy.tsx:155-162 decides the outcome copy from whether `signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` RESOLVED, and the comment at privacy.tsx:148-154 states that its failure 'is not swallowed' and that 'a thrown sign-out left the sentence on screen untrue'. That premise is false. apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:197-208 calls `signOutClosedAccount(...)` then `clearDeviceAdultSecrets()`; inside, apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:256-257 does `await effects.relockOnServer().catch(() => undefined)` and `await auth.signOut().catch(() => undefined)`, and apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:211-212 does `biometricPinStore.clear().catch(() => undefined)` and `forgetStoreIdentity().catch(() => undefined)` under a comment that says outright 'Both are best effort; neither may stop the sign-out'. On top of that apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:111-113 is `await client?.auth.signOut({scope:'local'})` and never looks at supabase-js's returned `{ error }`, which is how supabase reports a refused or failed sign-out (it does not throw). So every step that could leave the device not signed out is invisible to the caller: `signedOut` is true unless a SecureStore write in mode.ts:265 / unpairChildDevice threw. The fact the guard establishes is 'the keychain writes and navigation effects did not throw', not 'this device is signed out'.
findings.repro: Part 1 (exists today, green): apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.test.ts:156-166 'still signs out and clears when the device is offline (relock and remote sign-out fail)' passes `{ signOut: vi.fn(() => Promise.reject(new Error('offline'))) }` and `signOutParent` RESOLVES. Part 2 (new): in a suite that can stub apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts, assert `await signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` resolves when `parentAuth.signOut` rejects; therefore the ternary at privacy.tsx:161 takes `result.message`, i.e. ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed = 'Your PencilLift account is closed and this device is signed out.' A screen-level test would assert the shown message does not contain /this device is signed out/i after a failed sign-out, and it fails.
findings.user_impact: The round believed it had stopped the app telling a parent 'and this device is signed out' when it was not, and it has not: on the flaky-connection closure the comment names, the parent still reads that sentence, and the server-side adult-unlock relock and the store-identity forget silently did not happen. `accountClosedStillSignedInMessage` — a new exported function with six new assertions behind it — can now only be reached by a keychain write failure, never by a sign-out failure, so for its stated purpose it is built and not connected. The portal, which the comment cites as the parity case, actually verifies: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:744-750 re-reads `auth.currentSession()` and PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:814-820 only shows the still-signed-in copy when that read says a session is still held. The mobile side asserts the same distinction and does not perform it, so the L-037 parity claim in the comment is untrue.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked and none of these prevents it: (a) the new test apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:317-333 only greps privacy.tsx for `const signedOut = await signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` and for the ternary — it never runs the helper, so it stays green whatever the helper swallows; (b) parent-privacy.test.ts:300-315 only exercises the copy function on its own inputs; (c) mode.ts has no other path that surfaces an auth failure — line 257's `.catch(() => undefined)` is the only handler and parent-auth.ts:111-113 already dropped supabase's `{error}` before it; (d) apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:123-136 pins only that privacy.tsx calls the helper. I also confirmed the whole mobile suite is green at b802686 (760 passing), so nothing else is catching this.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the sign-out report what it did instead of inferring it from a resolved promise. Give `signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` a result — e.g. `Promise<{ sessionEnded: boolean; secretsCleared: boolean }>` — by having `parentAuth.signOut()` return supabase's `{ error }` (parent-auth.ts:111-113) and `signOutParent` pass that up instead of `.catch(() => undefined)` (mode.ts:257), and by returning the outcomes of the two best-effort clears (runtime.ts:211-212) rather than discarding them; keep the 'nothing may stop the sign-out' behaviour, only stop hiding the result. Then, mirroring the portal, re-read the session (`parentAuth.userId()` / a `getSession()` read) on the unverified path and choose the copy from that read, not from the absence of a throw. Fix the comments at privacy.tsx:144-154 and parent-privacy.ts:170-179 to say what is actually checked.

findings.title: Reordering the sign-out left the closed-account screen looking idle with every control, including a second "Delete my account", live
findings.requirement: APL-07 / PLAY-10 account deletion: the outcome of a closure must be shown, and a closed account must not accept another closure
findings.mechanism: privacy.tsx:138 clears the busy flag (`setBusy(null)`) as soon as the API answers, but the outcome state is now set only at privacy.tsx:159-162, AFTER `await signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` at privacy.tsx:155. Between them the screen is still `{status:'ready'}` with `data` non-null, so the whole 'Delete my account' section (privacy.tsx:465-501) renders with its button `disabled={busy !== null}` — i.e. enabled — and `feedback` was set to null at privacy.tsx:136, so nothing at all is on screen. That window is the length of the device sign-out, which is three network calls with no short timeout: `relockOnServer()` posts through the app's ApiClient whose default is DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000 (packages/contracts/src/client.ts:49), then `auth.signOut()` (parent-auth.ts:111-113), then `forgetStoreIdentity()` (runtime.ts:212). Before this diff `setState({status:'account_closed', ...})` ran first, which made `data` null (privacy.tsx:190) and removed the section immediately. A second tap re-enters `closeAccount` (privacy.tsx:134 sees `busy === null`, and `closeConfirmed` is never reset) and issues a second POST /v1/account/close, which the still-live token and still-recent unlock accept: apps/api/src/routes/account.ts:87-110 enqueues another close job and writes another `account.close_requested` audit row, and a second `signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` runs concurrently with the first.
findings.repro: Manual, throttled-network: on the privacy screen tick the confirmation and tap 'Delete my account' with the device on a stalled connection (so `relockOnServer` runs to the 20 s timeout). The button un-greys, no 'Account deleted' section appears, and tapping it again sends a second POST /v1/account/close (visible as two `account.close_requested` audit rows for the same user). Automated: extract the handler into src/privacy (it is pure but for the two injected effects) and drive it with `closeAccountAction` resolving `{status:'closed', message: ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed}` and a `signOut` that never settles; assert the busy key is still 'account' and that a second invocation is refused. Today neither holds.
findings.user_impact: A parent who has just deleted their account sees nothing happen for up to half a minute, with the red 'Delete my account' button live again, so the natural reaction — tap it again — sends a second closure, queues a second close job and writes a second audit row; a mis-tap on the neighbouring controls can also file a deletion request or open an export link for an account that is closing. The confirmation of the most destructive action in the app is the one thing that is now delayed.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked: (a) the only guard on re-entry is `if (!api || busy !== null) return;` at privacy.tsx:134 and busy is null after line 138, and the re-render triggered by setBusy(null) makes that visible to the next tap; (b) the close section's render condition is only `data ?` (privacy.tsx:465), and `data` stays non-null while the state is 'ready' (privacy.tsx:190), so nothing else hides it; (c) `closeConfirmed` is never reset after a successful close, so the second call passes `confirmed: true` and is not stopped by parent-privacy.ts:192; (d) the two new tests (parent-privacy.test.ts:317-333) only grep the source for the await and the ternary — they are satisfied by both the buggy and the fixed ordering — and no test in the mobile suite renders this screen (apps/mobile/vitest.config.ts includes only `src/**/*.test.ts`).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the screen busy across the whole operation: move `setBusy(null)` to after the `await signOutClosedAccountOnDevice()` (or set an explicit `{status:'closing'}` state before the await that renders the 'Account deleted' section with a 'Signing this device out…' line), so the section is gone or disabled for the duration and the parent gets immediate acknowledgement. While doing it, lift the handler into apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts with the sign-out injected, so this ordering can be unit-tested instead of grepped.

findings.title: The still-signed-in message tells the parent to change a password that no longer exists, and the new test pins that advice
findings.requirement: spec P14 / L-053: user-facing copy must be true and must point somewhere that works
findings.mechanism: parent-privacy.ts:185 ends both branches with '…and if you are worried, change your password from another device.' For `status === 'closed'` that is impossible: POST /v1/account/close answers 'closed' only after `closeNow` succeeded (apps/api/src/routes/account.ts:105-110, 180-193), which calls the auth admin adapter's soft delete — apps/api/src/providers/auth-admin.ts:19-21 and 65-78 document exactly what GoTrue does with `should_soft_delete: true`: 'the auth.users row (deleted_at set, email and phone replaced by hashes, metadata emptied, sessions ended)'. With the email hashed there is no sign-in and no password reset to perform, and ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.intro (packages/contracts/src/account.ts:48-49) says so itself: 'your email address and password stop working in the app and on the parent portal'. The advice is correct only on the 'pending' branch, where ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.ownerRule (account.ts:50-51) says the parent 'can still sign in to check on it'. The portal's sibling copy deliberately stops before that sentence: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:723-729 says only 'Use "Sign out" at the top of this page before you leave it.'
findings.repro: `accountClosedStillSignedInMessage('closed')` returns a string containing 'change your password from another device'. Following it: the parent opens the portal on another device, enters the closed email, and gets 'That email and password did not match' (apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:63-65) or requests a reset and no email ever arrives, because the auth user's email is a hash. A regression test asserts `accountClosedStillSignedInMessage('closed')` does NOT match /change your password/i while `('pending')` may.
findings.user_impact: A parent who has just been told the app could not sign this device out, and who is worried enough to act, is sent to do the one thing that cannot work — and spends that worry on a dead end instead of signing out from the parent menu, which is the step that actually helps.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked: (a) there is no branch in parent-privacy.ts:180-186 that omits the sentence — it is in the shared suffix, appended to both `closure` values; (b) the new test does not catch it, it enforces it: apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:300-314 loops over BOTH statuses and asserts `expect(message).toMatch(/change your password/i)` at line 312, so the untrue advice is pinned and a correct fix turns that test red; (c) 'closed' cannot mean 'the auth user is untouched' — account.ts:105-110 downgrades to 202 'pending' whenever `closeNow` returns false.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the password sentence from the 'closed' branch (keep it, if wanted, only for 'pending', where the sign-in is still open), and change parent-privacy.test.ts:312 to assert per status rather than for both. Keeping the actionable half — 'Sign out from the parent menu before you put it down' — matches the portal's wording at PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:723-729.

findings.title: 'nothing_to_cancel' repeats the premise error HUNT5-H-4 just fixed: a missing local assignment id is treated as "no scan exists"
findings.requirement: AC_CAPTURE_06 one job one charge / L-050: an idempotency path must not gate on the absence of a downstream event
findings.mechanism: upload.ts:286 returns 'nothing_to_cancel' whenever `attempt.assignmentId === null`, and upload.ts:339 gives that answer `keepAttempt: false`, so apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:283 rotates the idempotency keys and the child is told 'Stopped. Your pages are still here.' But `assignmentId` is only set by the `onAttempt` callback after the create RESPONSE is seen (upload.ts:210-211, scan.tsx:267-269). If the child taps 'Stop sending' while the create round trip is in flight, `cancellable` throws ScanCancelledError (upload.ts:126-134) before `onAttempt` ever runs, while the POST may well have committed server-side (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:763-767 inserts the row). So `assignmentId === null` establishes only 'this device never saw a create response', not 'no scan was created' — the same conflation the round fixed one branch away, where the cancel's absence of success was read as success. The consequence is the one HUNT5-H-4 argued against: the createKey that would have made the retry idempotent (homework.ts:736-745 returns the existing row for the same key) is discarded, so 'Try again' creates a SECOND assignment for the same homework and the first is orphaned.
findings.repro: Unit: `const a = newAttempt(newKey); expect(stoppedScanOutcome(await cancelScan(api, a)).keepAttempt).toBe(false)` — that is today's behaviour and today's assertion. The behavioural repro: run `uploadScan` with a `signal` aborted while the POST /v1/assignments promise is pending, so `onAttempt` is never called; then run the screen's abort branch and observe that `attemptRef.current` gets fresh keys, and a following `uploadScan` posts a different `idempotencyKey` for the same pages. A regression test asserts the createKey survives a stop taken before the create response arrived.
findings.user_impact: A child on a slow connection who taps Stop during the first second of a send, then taps Try again, leaves a duplicate scan behind: the first assignment stays in their own list (GET /v1/child/assignments has no status filter, apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1416-1420) showing 'Not sent yet — This scan hasn't finished sending' (apps/mobile/src/homework/result-view.ts:104-111) for ever, next to the one that actually went. No double charge — finalize is the authoritative reservation (homework.ts:757-759) — so the harm is a phantom scan and a burned create against the child's 30/hour limit (homework.ts:117), not money.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked: (a) nothing else preserves the key — scan.tsx:283 rotates on `!outcome.keepAttempt` and there is no other keeper; (b) `changePages` (scan.tsx:125-131) also rotates, so no later path recovers it; (c) the case is not covered by the 'unsure' fix, because cancelScan returns before its try block when the id is null (upload.ts:286); (d) the existing test does not catch it, it asserts it: apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.test.ts:598-607 loops `['cancelled','nothing_to_cancel']` under the title 'a scan that really was stopped keeps the calm "Stopped" copy and a fresh attempt' and asserts `keepAttempt).toBe(false)` at line 601 — 'nothing_to_cancel' is not a scan that really was stopped; (e) I searched docs/Bug_Ledger.md and docs/Lessons_Learned.md for 'nothing_to_cancel' and there is no record of this residual.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the attempt whenever a scan may exist. Cheapest: have `stoppedScanOutcome('nothing_to_cancel')` return `keepAttempt: true` — reusing an unused createKey is harmless, and `changePages` already rotates the keys whenever the pages change, so a retained key can never belong to a different page set. Cleaner: distinguish 'the create never left this device' (the signal aborted before the POST, upload.ts:178) from 'no response was seen' and give only the former a fresh attempt; the latter should keep the keys and, if the copy must differ, say what 'unsure' says. Update upload.test.ts:598-607 accordingly.

findings.title: The new function was inserted between `closeAccountAction` and its JSDoc, leaving a stranded doc block and an undocumented function
findings.requirement: L-053: prose and code must not disagree

Nothing is sent until the parent has ticked the confirmation; the server needs a recent PIN unlock…') documents `closeAccountAction`. findings.title: `cancelScan` can no longer reject, so the `.catch` on the page-change cancel is dead code a reader will take for live
findings.mechanism: After this diff `cancelScan` has no throwing path: upload.ts:286 is the only statement outside the try and it cannot throw, and the catch at upload.ts:295-298 now returns 'unsure' instead of rethrowing (the diff replaced `throw error;`). The abort path was updated accordingly — scan.tsx:282 dropped its `.catch` — but scan.tsx:127 still reads `void cancelScan(childApi, previous).catch(() => undefined);`. That handler can never run. It also still discards the answer, so a 'too_late' or 'unsure' on a page change is silently thrown away, which is the shape HUNT5-H-4 was filed about even though the outcome here (the pages changed, so a new scan is correct) is benign.

So the rejection handler at scan.tsx:127 is unreachable; a coverage run over scan.tsx shows the arrow at 127 never executing under any input.

It misleads the next reader in the specific way this round was burned by: the `.catch` at scan.tsx:127 says 'this call can fail', so a reader adding a third caller will copy a handler that does nothing, or conclude the abort path at scan.tsx:282 is missing one.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked: (a) upload.ts:282-299 is the whole function and the `api.send` call is inside the try, so even a synchronous throw from the client becomes a caught rejection; (b) there is no other `cancelScan` caller (I grepped the mobile tree: scan.tsx:127 and scan.tsx:282 only); (c) no test asserts on that `.catch` — apps/mobile/src/homework/scan-screen.test.ts:75-84 only checks that `catch(() => 'cancelled'` is gone and that the abort-path call has no handler.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `.catch(() => undefined)` at scan.tsx:127 (keep the `void`), or, if the answer is worth acting on, branch on it the way the abort path now does. Either way say in one line that `cancelScan` answers rather than throws, so the asymmetry with scan.tsx:282 does not read as an omission.

sweeps_sound: The 'unsure' copy points somewhere that works: 'Check My scans to see if it went' (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:335) is answerable, because GET /v1/child/assignments filters on child only, not status (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1416-1420), and a draft/uploading row renders as 'Not sent yet — This scan hasn't finished sending. Open Scan to send it again' (apps/mobile/src/homework/result-view.ts:104-111). Tried to show the child would be told nothing, or told a never-sent scan had gone; could not.

keepAttempt: true on 'unsure' really is idempotent in all three server states: the same createKey returns the existing row (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:736-745), a cancelled/deleted row raises ScanStoppedError which the screen handles (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:219-221 with apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:285-288), and a finalized row reports as sent without touching pages (upload.ts:215-218). No path produces a second assignment.

'Stop means stop: the server releases anything reserved for this scan' (apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:275) holds: POST /v1/assignments/:id/cancel releases `usage_reservations` and cancels queued/failed_retryable `jobs` for that scan (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1077-1084), and 'queued' is cancellable (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:149-156).

Removing the `.catch` at apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:282 cannot produce an unhandled rejection inside `send()`'s catch block: `cancelScan` (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:282-299) has only one statement outside its try and it cannot throw.

The cancel is not killed by the abort that triggered it: `cancelScan` calls `api.send` with no RequestOptions (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:288-293), so the aborted AbortSignal is never attached.

The new `abortBranch` extraction is not vacuous: the anchor regex matches apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:274 through 285 (6-space `} else if`, the only one in the file) and apps/mobile/src/homework/scan-screen.test.ts:92 guards with `expect(abortBranch).not.toBe('')`, so a branch that stops matching turns the test red rather than green. This is a real repair of the previous 400-character tautology.

The negative assertion at apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:308 searches the right string: ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed and .pending both contain the exact phrase 'this device is signed out' (packages/contracts/src/account.ts:59-61). L-054's string check holds here.

The `ApiRequestError('NETWORK','offline',0,'TIMEOUT')` fixture at apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.test.ts:631-634 is the shape the real client produces: the constructor is (code, message, status, rule) (packages/contracts/src/client.ts:10-15) and a timeout is raised as NETWORK with rule NETWORK_RULES.timeout = 'TIMEOUT', status 0 (client.ts:52, 96). Not a state reachable only by a route no user can take.

scripts/test-minimums.json's raised floors do not make CI red, and nothing in this diff ships red or skipped: I ran each suite with a non-writing reporter — mobile 760 passed (floor 722), web 780 passed (floor 741), api 1128 passed (floor 1071) — and `tsc -p apps/mobile/tsconfig.json` exits 0. The floors sit below the real counts, which matches the pre-existing pattern (mobile was 701 against ~738), so this is a floor, not a drifted equality.

J-mobile-privacy-scan.notes:
Verification I actually ran (read-only): the full mobile suite (760 passed, 0 failed/skipped), the web suite (780) and the api suite (1128), each with `npx vitest run --reporter=dot` so no test-results JSON was written, plus `tsc -p apps/mobile/tsconfig.json` (clean). I did not run the db suite (needs Postgres), so the 383→400 floor in scripts/test-minimums.json is unverified; the other three floors are below their real counts.

What I could not check. Everything device-only: whether ImageManipulator, expo-secure-store or the RevenueCat logout actually fail in the ways HUNT6-J-1 and HUNT6-J-2 depend on, and how long they take on a real flaky connection. apps/mobile/app/(parent)/privacy.tsx and app/(child)/scan.tsx cannot be rendered by this suite at all (vitest.config.ts includes only `src/**/*.test.ts`), so every "test" over them in my area is a source grep — which is precisely how HUNT6-J-1 and HUNT6-J-2 passed review: apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:317-333 pins the SHAPE of the new code and can never observe that the helper it calls swallows the failure the fix is about, or that the outcome is now shown after a long await.

Two weaknesses I judged not to be findings. (1) apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.test.ts:308's `not.toMatch(/this device is signed out/i)` searches a string the function builds locally without that phrase, so it can only fail if someone pastes the phrase in; the coupling that matters — ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY being reworded so the phrase no longer appears there either — is unasserted. The other four assertions in that test do pin real copy, so I left it. (2) apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:322's parenthetical "'unsure' — the cancel itself never reached the server" is untrue for a 429 or 404, which did reach it; the function doc at upload.ts:275-280 gets this right ("cannot know whether the server stopped the scan") and the child-facing message is honest either way, so it is one loose clause rather than a defect.

One narrow hazard I decided not to file. Because 'unsure' now keeps the keys, a cancel that failed because the assignment was deleted (404, e.g. a parent deletion in flight) locks the child onto a createKey that the create will answer with CONFLICT for ever (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:740-743 throws when `row.status === 'deleted'`), and the else branch at apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:289-292 keeps the attempt, so every "Try again" shows the generic message with no escape but editing the page list. It needs a deletion to land in the same second as the stop, and the same trap predates this diff on the ordinary error path, so I recorded it here rather than as a finding.

Sibling surface outside my files, for whoever owns it: SignOutButton (apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:488-499) calls `signOutParentOnDevice()` and reports nothing either (`.finally(() => setBusy(false))`), so the remedy HUNT6-J-3's copy sends the parent to has the same unverified outcome as the closure path — the same L-037 question one screen over.
